These were costly, (The Nightrider car is $5mil.)
Now Gunrunning released. Major powercreep here. Explosive Heavy Sniper Rifle makes planes pretty weak within combat. You had vehicles which you could upgrade to be more resilient to damage and protective of your fleshy body. These vehicles aren't cheap either. The upgrades were locked behind research, researched can use stock you can steal to do overtime, or you can fast-track the research, which for the first is $100k, then $225k for the rest. (Fast-Tracking can reduce all the research into a 3hr time period). These items can dominate a game if used by a group of competent people.
Now the new update as of writing this: Smuggler's Run. Oh boy, what do I have to say? Except it's of subpar quallity to previous updates. Yes the previous update had problems, but even that update was better. The planes aren't worth the money, even when upgraded. Balance is another problem with this update, the planes are fairly low damage, unless you're a fan of homing missles on the planes. A Hydra is a straight upgrade to them, and that already exists in the game, and is considerably cheaper since you don't have to buy a hangar to store it. The hanger's money making system is the same as Special Cargo. Build up supplies by grabbing bits and sell bulk. Except unlike special cargo you can only get 1 crate of goods at a time, which is worth $10k. Special Cargo is worth twice the money (If you go use the Large Special Cargo Warehouse). And you can gather up to 3 at once. Also, the update is buggy, but that's to be expected. The update on a whole appears to be rushed. Compared to Import/Export and Gunrunning, this DLC doesn't have missions to reduce price of the vehicles, that's an unlock of just doing supply runs. That is a downgrade as the missions were actually fun, the supply runs not that fun, in this update actually really fustrating. You shoot down the enemy and more enemies spawn constantly throughout the mission. It's tedious at best. It's also worth considering that this update's stuff at the best options costs $30 million in total. If you bought the cash cards that's £240 worth of cash cards to get this stuff... O.o
If anything, I hate to say that Rockstar has made a hash of the current update. As this update is more buggy than Gunrunning was on release. The supply missions are tedious at best. On the whole, this update isn't fun. GTA Online as the entire thing is a boring grind-fest. You need money if you want to have fun with things like the Half-Track. And I'd dare say that modders that actually drop money for others make the game a more of a balanced experience. Not everyone has the time and/or funds to unlock the expensive content.
TL:DR; GTA Online is a grind fest to get the good things. Unbalanced, and possibly contains Pay-2-Win elements.

Torchlight II is an action/RPG/hack n' slash game set in an extremely colorful and fictional world. I played the first game on the Xbox and absolutely loved it, and in many ways, Torchlight II picks up the slack where the first game didn't.
In terms of story, both gams are lacking. MINOR SPOILER:
Along the way, you will find sidequests and bosses to fight that will help you level up so you can defeat the next boss, level up, defeat the next boss, etc. While this main seem boring and repetitive, in the eight hours I've played the game Torchlight II has never felt tedious or exhausting. (Only recently it has become slightly annoying due to enemies called Sandrats that are SO HARD TO KILL.) Other than that, the bosses always offer up a new spin and are just enough to keep you on your toes.
Where Torchlight II shines from its predecessor is the revamped menus. It's so easy to find loot and determine if it's better than yours or not, find if weapons do more damage than the one you have, etc. You also have the ability to have two sets of weapons. (I prefer having a ranged set and a melee set, but do whatever you want if you buy this.) The customization of characters is fairly extensive, especially with the added pets you can have to help you. And I must say, the pets are EXTREMELY helpful.
Other small fixes include better warning systems on Trapped Chests. (Fans of the first game will get what I mean,) as well as more mana abilites that will allow you to take out several enemies at once, and also some very wide open areas where you can free people from slave caravans, take on monsters, and if you're lucky, find a Phase Beast that will give you a Phase Portal. (Warning: Entering a Phase Portal will take you to a fairly challenging arena battle, but the loot is incredible.)
My only complaint about Torchlight II, and this may just be a glitch for me, but recently I have been collecting loot that is WAY out of my level range. I don't know if I missed a couple of sidequests that would have pushed me to a higher level to get better equipment. I wouldn't think they would make the sidequests necessary for leveling up in the main quests, because they are supposed to be bonus things for XP and so on.
10/10
Better Than Torchlight
Fun And Challenging
May Get Repetitive
Minor Leveling Issues
I hope this review helps you make your decision!

As a big Scribblenauts fan since the original for the Nintendo DS, I looked forward to this game. Adding to the large dictionary the previous iterations had to offer, the developers add almost every DC character- an impressive acomplishment. You can still screw around in a sandbox world, just like in the previous games, writing anything. The only problem is that your sandbox doesn't save your progress when you exit, however, which can be annoying since there is already the manual option for resetting.
A (somewhat) new feature was the hero creator. In short, it's Scribblenauts Unlimited's object editor in which you could edit any existing object, but with the ability to add super powers. Additionally, Unmasked introduced a combat system. Right clicking would activate your built in powers, or otherwise, a punch from your character. If you add more than one ability, it's kind of inconsistant on which ability will appear. Often times, my heat rays will shoot everything, and my green lantern punches were nowhere to be found. The superpowers are neat, but they feel difficult to use.
Something I should also point out is that the charming Scribblenauts music from the previous games did not return. It was a bit depressing not to hear the familiar songs, but eventually you don't bother to really care about the music anyway.
The puzzles in this game felt like a combination between the first Scribblenauts puzzles with Unlimited's puzzles. They aren't perfect though. After about two hours, you'll find the same recurring puzzles, which makes you want to stay in the sandbox batcave. The biggest problem though, is that sometimes, I could enter a world, let my character stand there, and immediately, somehow automatically get an achievement. You'll soon take notice that it's due to the puzzle givers intertwining paths, killing each other because "Heroes V.S. Villains". I understand the developers had put effort into keeping all the puzzle givers into one world, but it didn't end up working.
Even though Scribblenauts may be losing its color, it's still a very unique game. Fighting with/against the DC characters in their adventures makes you want to read the comics.  In some ways, Scribblenauts Unmasked excelled in areas its predecessors could not handle. In other ways, this game went back some steps. Despite all this, it won't stop me from continuing to beat up Batman with my bare fists.

Before we get into the review, a disclaimer on this one: I'm writing this under the assumption you, potential reader, are interested in a "clicker" game, where a "clicker" game is a game that exists to just keep clicking things and raising values until you finally get some kind of reward. In this game, that reward is a girl's affections.
I mistakenly downloaded this game as it was tagged "visual novel," which is how I stumbled onto it, and ended up playing it for a while. Make no mistake, though, it isn't a visual novel by any means. However, if you are interested in this title as a "clicker" game, then keep reading. If not, then I can't say I actually do recommend it.
With that awkward introduction out of the way, let's get to it.
As a "clicker" game, you will find yourself going through expected motions. You click on a button, wait a while after seeing a number go up, then click on the button again, and repeat.  The main goal is for the affection of multiple girls. You start with one, but unlock more as you go on.
The art is decent for what the game is and the music fits for what you'll be doing. Charming department store type music would be my best description. In terms of its story, the premise is actually pretty charming, even if the writing isn't really substantial enough to go anywhere at all with it.
Initially, you have a limited amount of time blocks available, which limits how much you can do in real time, but you unlock more as you progress. This is actually a decent system, and the game isn't too harsh about doling these out to you, at least for the time I played.
The game also grants you affection as time goes on once you meet certain stat requirements, which is a good plus. In fact, once you get things set up, you can basically just quit the game, because it racks up everything for up to a week of real life time even if you're not playing.
That one thing is, truth be told, the main reason I would recommend this game. Without that, it becomes a senseless clicker like all the rest I've seen. With that feature, though, combined with another feature it has, it actually is a lot more approachable than I first suspected it to be.
The other feature it has is called Prestige. Although the game doesn't explain it clearly/early enough for my liking, the idea behind it is if you reset your current progress with the girls, you can keep all your money and stats and start over. The thing you get in exchange for this is that you get money and affection faster than before. It's a novel idea, and works pretty well to make the player feel like they wasting their time.
And at a glance, the player is going to feel like they're wasting their time.
What do I mean?
The first level gift costs $400. The fifth costs over $15,000. The second level gift costs $1,000 and grants 64 affection points. Soon enough it goes into hundreds of thousands. Even when characters hate you, you can get 25 points every ten seconds for free. Working the first job for a whike will get you around $10 (based on promotions, first less and then more) every four seconds.
The short of it is that this game is designed to be left on and to its own devices once you get it going, which is unlike most "clicker" titles I've come across. If I had any major complaint here, as a "clicker" player anyway (which I can't actually say I am), it would be that these things aren't made clear off the bat. Maybe that's for the better? I can't say.
tl;dr:
To me, "clicker" games are hard not to immediately describe as time wasters, and although this one does do some things that impress me as far as the "genre" is concerned, it's still hard not to feel that way. Despite that, not only will I probably keep poking at it, since this genre is notorious for bringing out the addictive side of people, but if I'm fair about that, all games are time wasters in a way.
In the end, all I can say is this. If this is the kind of waste of time you like, then this is shaping up to be an alright example of that type of time killer, and it might just be one you can enjoy and get a whole lot out of.
So give it a shot and see if you like it. Maybe you'll find yourself in the arms of the love of your life by the end. Who knows?

Strania is yet another Xbox 360 shmup release that is seeing new life on the Steam platform. As far as those releases go, this was my favorite along with Eschatos (also on Steam, and something you should also buy if you haven't yet). What I appreciated the most about this game was G.Rev's decision to design it will respect to the "Traditional" style shooter, as opposed to the bullet hell style which has become more common in modern shump design. Not to say I don't like to play bullet hells, I just prefer the design elements of the 80's/early 90's shooters, where the focus was on less numerous but more targeted bullets, an assortment of distinct weapons to use where success in the game is determined by proper use of said weapons in different situations, environmental hazards, cinematic style stage progression, etc. Think Gradius, R-Type, Thunder Force, the various Complie shooters like MUSHA, and Einhander as examples of what this is modeled after. That type of style is right up my alley, and Strania does the job of scratching that particular itch. Add on top of that, add the catchy, shump appropriate, electro synth fusion soundtrack of Keishi Yonao, and you have a very well crafted game.
The craftsmanship extends to the fact that G.Rev took it upon themselves to make a whole extra addition to main Strania campaign with the "Side Vover" add on (at no extra cost in the Steam version), were you play the game from the perspective of the Stranian antagonists, the Vower. Essentially, you play the main game in reverse, starting from the Vower home colony, going through the same stages from the Strania side to get the Stranian home base. However, instead of being the recycled affair you would likely expect from something like this, the stage design, bosses, music, and progression is distinct enough to make it feel like an entirely different game. It was an example of how to do DLC the right way, by adding value to the game while keeping the main portion whole and untampered with.
Those that are more observant will see the subtleties that G.Rev put in both campaigns to differentiate the Stranian and Vower sides, and give them personality without even having to rely on story composition. For example, the Stranian's mechs and infrastructure are very angular and blocky and the uniforms of the main pilots suggest a militaristic, organized culture. The Vower's mechs and equipment on the other hand, are mostly rounded and curved, and the dress of the pilots suggest a tribal, nomadic, theocratic culture. Another example is that while pilots on both sides can use each others weapon arrays (denoted by being highlighted by Blue (Strania), Red (Vower) or Purple (Netural) in game), only mechs on the Stranian side have access to enhanced versions of the Strania side's weapons (essentially activated by collecting two of the same weapon on one weapon slot), and only Vower mechs can use enhanced Vower weapons on the other end. Depending on what side you play, you'll find that the enemies will mostly attack you with their side's weapons, which you mainly get from stealing them off destroyed enemy mechs. Weapons on your side are mainly gotten by storage crates and friendly drops. It's the little things that help make this game special.
If you are a fan of the genre at all, don't make the mistake of overlooking this game, as it apparently was when it was initially released. It deserves more recognition, and is a much purchase. And you definitely want G.Rev releasing more of their games on Steam.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding cheese cake recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1 cup digestive plain sweet biscuit crumbs
3 tablespoons sugar
3 tablespoons melted butter
40 ounces softened cream cheese
1 cup sugar
3 tablespoons flour
1 tablespoon vanilla
1 cup sour cream
4 eggs
Directions:
For The base:.
If you're using a dark pan, preheat the oven to 350. If you are using a shiny pan, 375.
Combine the crumbs, melted butter and 3 tbsp sugar well and pat onto the bottom of a 9 inch springform pan. I also like to very very lightly butter the sides of the pan so that the cheesecake will not stick later on.
Bake for 10 mins in your preheated oven and remove. Let it cool while you prepare your batter.
For the batter:.
Make sure everything is at room temperature.
Combine sugar, cheese, flour and vanilla in a big bowl and mix on medium speed till well combined. Don't forget to scrape the bowl as you're doing this.
Mix in the sour cream till its incorporated well. Then, add the eggs one by one, mixing well after each addition.
Pour the batter into the springform and let it bake for 1 hour and 10 minutes After the baking time, turn off the oven and leave the door ajar. Let the cake cool in there for about 1 1/2 hours.
Remove the cake and let it cool thoroughly. Refrigerate overnight.
Release the sides of the springform.
Eat.

As an arcade game it's Okay, but personally I thing it's a bit of a joke refering to this game as a 'Simulator'.
This game does give a basic but fairly decent idea of how sea rescues are often carried out. Graphics are nice but for some reason are  unusually heavy on RAM for what you get, resulting in a poor frame rate for something that doesn't appear particularly high-spec.
Controls are pretty rubbish to be honest, these would certainly benefit from having a precise control feature, such as with V-Step's Ship Simulator series, and the boats acutually reponding better to control input, particularly when going astern (reversing).
Physics could do with some fine-tuning, such as the boats being less bouncy over waves that don't appear particularly big or rough, also the afore mentioned poor controls go hand-in-hand with these below-par physics, especially in the case of the smaller daughter-boats.
Have also come across at least one bug. The first being that the already poor controls bring it on themselves to go full ahead on the throttles and full to port (left) on the steering, any atempt to correct them, either by using the keyboard or click-dragging the mouse only working until buttons are released. Sometimes this bug takes affect at the start of gameplay, sometimes only taking affect in the middle of gameplay.
As a spare time arcade game this is okay, but on the whole it's got potential but in need of a great deal of improvement. Taking all into consideration I honestly can't say I recommend this.

The game isn't poorly optimized. I have a midrange system of a Radeon 380, 8 gbs of ram, and an i5 4560 processor. I get a steady frame rate on high at every point despite these unimpresive stats. While initial loading screens are longer, more of the world is accessible without loading screens. You can walk through the vast majority of the hub without any delay. This includes all interior buildings one of which is a multi-level bank.
The game is not "cut in half." Average playtime acroding to numerous online stat websites puts this game at longer than Human Revolution. While there is only a single HUB, it's a wonderfully realized worldspace. I've spent hours jumping from balcony to balcony and trying to hack and infiltrate my way through a bank. The side quest are well written and flesh out the world in a meaningful way. The side quest also allow you to continue the search for answers into lingering questions of Adam Jensen's mysterious past and the conspiracies around him. Level design is far more open than Human Revolution and stealth is more than a "find that predetermined path" and requires clever use of Augmentations and improvsation.
If users want to give negative reviews for bad business practices such as microtransactions and high priced 30 dollars season pass that's fine, but you should know that the core experience here is a large improvement over Human Revolution.

I'm giving this a 'thumbs down' not because it's a complete disaster.  It's not.  The game is stable, free of obvious bugs, and it is somewhat engaging for the first couple of hours.  Let me run through the first challenge as a case study:
You get a call that some one is in trouble.  You put the pedal to the metal and head toward the arrow which indicates where the people are who need rescuing.
You realize very quickly that this is taking a long time.  Ten minutes in fact.  That's ten minutes of doing nothing but holding down the 'w' key.  I discovered later that there's an option that doubles the speed; so reduce the time to five minutes of holding the 'w' key.
[Edit] Greanthal pointed out that I could go at 4X speed.  I didn't remember that option so I returned to the game and headed out to sea.  Under menu there are several speed options one of which is 'fastest'.  This is what I had clicked before and got 2X speed.  So I clicked it again and got the same result.  What I didn't realize was that 'fastest' is not 'fastest'.  If you click the option again you get 4X.  I guess it means 'fastest acceleration'.
[Edit] This does not save the game from my thumbs down rating however.  In the third mission under the Baltic senario, it still takes 7 minutes at 4X to reach the rescue destination.
Once you arrive on the scene you perform a couple of tasks including pulling three people out of the water.  This all takes less time than it took to get there.
Now you discover you have to take the rescued people back to port . . . another five minutes of holding the 'w' key.  You get back to port and you find out you have to return to the damaged boat . . . another five minutes of holding the 'w' key.
Back at the rescue site you attach a rope to the boat (takes about a minute) and you turn around to head back to port . . . another five minutes of holding down the 'w' key.  I think you get the picture.
Among other issues I have is that you can't turn off the music.  It's integrated with the master volume.  The music is louder in the menus but still in the background while travelling back and forth holding down the 'w' key.
Also, the claim about the wonderful water physics is a gross exaggeration.  I spent most of my childhood on the water, including open sea.  The water in this game barely resembles anything I've experienced.  A passing boat makes a deep furrow which lingers for an unnaturally long time; it looks more like a large furrow left by a tractor and plow ('plough' if you're outside North America).  Worse is that your boats do not interact with these 'furrows'.  You practically hover as you pass over them; not so much as a slight dip.
Some one in a review said it might be a $15 title.  I'd say it's barely worth it at $10.

NOTE: This review only covers the single player content of Grand Theft Auto V.
What can be said about Grand Theft Auto V that you already don't know? This game is an absolute masterpiece that shows why the series is the father and king of the open world genre. For me, it's definitely one the best videogames that i ever played. I played it to 100%, and except for when i was hunting for collectables, i enjoyed every minute of it. What sets this game apart for the competition is the obsessive attention to detail in everything. You can see the effort put in creating this masterpiece. The story isn't as engaging as past GTA titles, but still manages to be pretty good and well written, with interesting characters, especially the main trio. Playing with 3 different charactes brings some freshness, even if they mostly play the same. The motion capture and voice acting work are great, making the cutscenes cinematic in a good way. Personally, i didn't found the soundtrack to be that good, and lacked some variety. The gameplay, however, is pretty good, from shooting to driving, and during most of the minigames and extra activities. The mission variety is good, even if the game is easier than past titles. The checkpoint and especially the mission replay systems are more than welcome. The map has the right size, but it could be better designed, especially in the country areas. It didn't felt like forests or deserts, but a big mountainous area that lacked variety. And the game is missing casino minigames and the freaking jetpack! That was awesome in San Andreas, and it's absence here is disappointing. It's interesting that for me, what i didn't like here wasn't the game's flaws, but the lack of some content. The game is big and packed with quality content, so it's normal what i wanted even more. Even without Grand Theft Auto Online, this game easily deserves the full price.
I also need to point out that the PC version is great. The game is superbly optimized for a lot of systems, and even on low end machines it'll look great. The new first player perspective may feel like a bonus, but at 60 FPS and on a keyboard and mouse is a great way perphaps not to play (i recommend using the normal camera the first time you play the game) but to replay this amazing masterpiece. The PC version is clearly superior.

Scribblenauts Unmasked is a truly wonderful game. The Scribblenauts series is this: you have a notebook and puzzles. You write objects into your notebook and use them to solve puzzles. In Super Scribblenauts, you can add adjectives to the objects. In Scribblenauts Unlimited, you solve more puzzles with more objects to create and customize. Finally, in Scribblenauts Unmasked, you can create objects and people from the DC universe, and the game is shaped like a comic book. This is recommended for anyone who wants to test their imagination.
10/10.

Scribblenauts Unmasked is a great game. In a way, it's educational because you'll try to remember words you used to know, and it also makes you think of objects you usually have no connection with, or that only existed in your imagination.
But as the title suggests it's all about the DC universe so if you hate comic books you probably won't be able to enjoy yourself with this game. or at least not as much.
So, there are multiple worlds to visit; Gotham City, Metropolis and worlds connected to other DC characters like Aquaman or Wonder Woman. The levels are pretty big, and there are always multiple random objectives/quests to finish, and one story segment to complete. Modifiers can also be activated (like only writing words starting with the letter N) that earn you extra points. These points are used to play origin stories or other levels. You'll need to unlock all levels in order to be able to complete the game (which should take you somewhere between 10-15 hours, depending on how much you want to complete). Earning points, however, happens very fast and it will never take long before you can go the next area.
Scribblenauts Unmasked is basically the same as the previous Scribblenauts games, but with a different theme. This time it's a theme I usually adore. But writing and thinking of words is what it's really all about. And that's not bad. Not bad at all. In fact, I had a very fun time with it, but I do wonder if it can keep your attention long enough...
I would highly recommend it personally.

OK, I like the game. I really do. It's just that .. there are too many little dots, combined they form a hole. The game starts out well. It's very simple, which I think is a good thing. Controlling two characters at the same time was fun. There were great moments every now and then. But It doesn't keep its pace to the end. Or maybe it does, and that's what's wrong with it.
The pace the game takes is easy, slow, and just sweet. But that's it. There's no progression, no development within the game. To add to that, it is so short. You don't notice the lack of content until you are surprised that the game itself has ended. :/ for a 2 hours and a half game, to be so simple and straight forward, even with an empty story... And Especially with that ending!
I think this is a perfect example of how " simple " could be " way too simple " and become a negative aspect.
With that said, I loved the art style. visually, the game is breath taking " despite it being undemanding ". The voices are wonderful, mainly the music. The lack of actual language is a strong point, as everything happens as it is. It feels as if you're on a trip, watching the wild life. You don't understart the communication. Arguably, communication doesn't exist. But you watch, and you understand. and everything is just beautiful, like pieces of puzzle completing the whole picture.
There are many things that happen, because they just do. They feel natural, despite them being superficial, which is wonderful !
I think my main problems with the game are :
1: It is way too short.
2: It is way too plain. I didn't feel the plot, at all. Everything was predictable. I saw it coming miles away. I'm not asking for surprises just for the sake of them, but I don't ask to eat a plain empty bread either.
3: The story, oh my god the story. They just picked a very sad theme, everything way too plain and dry.
You know.. Just because your story is sad, doesn't mean it is good.
I'm just annoyed at the wasted opportunity, the game could have gone a VERY LONG WAY.
Oh well.

Get it on sale, Have fun. But don't take it seriously. The story is unnecessarily sad for no reason really. It shouldn't have been sad in my opinion. Or it could have had more depth to it. But it's an ok. nothing more, just an ok.

First note, that despite the very suggestive title, this is not associated with the game Ship Simulator Extremes that you can also buy on steam, and is developed by a different company. This is both a good and bad thing - it's good because there are many, many fewer graphical bugs and general slowness than you get from the classic ship simulator, but it has problems that I'll get into later.
My biggest concern with the game is the ship physics. They just don't feel right - a long endurance rescue vessel seems more like a small boat, and the boat feels terrible at low speeds, because of how it moves in the wrong direction when trying to steer. This might be realistic, but it sure doesn't seem like it.
Secondly, there's a distinct lack of content. There are only a few other ship classes, and cargo ships are represented by fishing boats etc. It gets annoying, but not too badly. Given the nature of the ships that they've modelled, a true open ocean scenario would be wonderful.
Third, the towing and cable attachment walkaround system is way, way too slow, even in calm seas.
I actually rather like this game. Poor ship physics aside, the campaign is at least okay, and there is a fair amount of diversity. However, it isn't quite worth 25$ - if it was 15$, I'd say you should buy it, but not at the current pricing. I hope that the developers continue to expand the content that's avaliable, though I'm not too hopeful.
Edit (too long for a comment):
I think that the easiest one of my complaints to fix is the walk-around one, I suspect that there's just a constant somewhere that can be changed.
The motor launch dynamics also need to be improved, as the sliding action when attempting to turn at low speeds makes it difficult to perform rescues effectively. However, this might be a realisim thing, as I have very little real experience with these boats.
The thing that I'd like the most to be added, content-wise, is an open-ocean component, far distant from the shore. The Hermann Marwede in particular was designed for this, and it doesn't show up a lot in the game. This would also go well with the addition of the emergency towing vessel Mellum, also based on  Heligoland.
Only one real new ship class is needed for freighters, really, and I think that something like a 5,000TEU containerized vessel would be enough. I'm not sure how hard it would be to add, though.
With respect to the missions, something that's been bothering me about the ones that exist already is that they're so close to shore and in good enough weather that the majority would seem to be done by helicopter. It would be nice to make you cooperate with a helicopter, possibly even conducting air operations off of the Marwede.
Finally, a mod kit would be very nice. VSTEP doesn't have one, for reasons I can't determine, but I know that I would be interested at least in developing new content for the game.
I think that implementing any two of my suggestions would make me, at least, reccomend this game. I'm excited to see where the game goes in the future.
Edit #2:
The ship physics are really the worst thing, though. The ships's weight more or less does not exist (the RHIB pushes a 5000 ton freighter around), and the boyancy model is nonexistent. Floating appears to happen based on a uniform height above the water. Furthermore, the drag model doesn't work: when you have a ship under tow, the top speed does not decrease whatsoever.

A non-biased quick look @ the game:
If it's one think the Japanese do best, it's make awesome SHUMP's. Japanese boutique game studio G.rev makes its long-awaited debut on Steam with Strania!
This throwback robot shoot’em up is an ode to the nostalgia of 1980s arcade games. Players will need to make strategic decisions quickly in this fast-paced, exhilarating shooter. Accompanied by a catchy soundtrack and featuring dramatic visual effects, G.rev proudly presents Strania as its first title on the Steam platform.
The Steam version of Strania includes the “Side Vower” DLC that was released separately for home consoles. Play as a pilot in the Vower camp that seeks to reclaim the land they hold sacred.  - Highly Recommended!

From modern STG pioneers G.rev, Strania takes its root deep into games such as Cybattler, MUSHA Aleste, Spriggan Mk II and other 90's mech shooters, while adding the mesmerizing and cinematic experience typical to G.rev that can be seen in some of their other titles such as Border Down or Under Defeat.
With collaboration from Treasure's former employee Hiroshi Iuchi as graphic designer, famous for directing games such as Radiant Silvergun and Ikaruga, and an exhilarating soundtrack with sharp sound effects produced by Keishi Yonao (Asuka 120%, Mad Stalker, Neural Gear), Strania is an accessible shooter that focuses more on environmental aspects rather than just throwing a million bullets at you on a lifeless terrain.
The controls are some of the tightest I've ever played, and the scoring system relying on weapon leveling is a very dynamic way of spicing things up for those wishing to push further their scores. The fans of more bullet-heavy games will also enjoy its expert mode with suicide bullets, and overall this game will definitely give a fair deal of challenge for all kind of skill levels.
If you're a fan of shooters, retro mechs and dramatic audio-visuals, this is the game for you.
Highly recommended!

Mechs, lots of weapons, and big explosions!  The gameplay video on Steam pretty much says it all, and it plays just as good as it looks.
The most interesting thing about this game is the variety in both the environment, enemy placement and design, and the way you handle each situation with the different weapons.  This is a game that rewards experimentation and replaying with different combinations.  You can switch on the fly and keep something in reserve, so each time I make a mistake I always think "oh yeah, I should try it like this instead".  Very fun if you like to go in-depth with the available options.
The recharging shield is also a cool dual-purpose tool.  You can use it for quick bursts of invincibility during a tricky section, or use it to boost multiplier during particularly lucrative situations.  It's up to you; play it safe or balls to the wall.
The graphics are a good compromise between awesomeness and visibilty.  There's streams of shell casings flying out of weapons (even though they shoot lasers), sweet but brief boss intros firing flak everywhere, and of course the deeply satisfying mega explostions when you down giant bosses.  Color choice is done well, so no matter how much is going on I haven't had visibility issues with bullets or the hitbox.

From the makers of Border Down, Under Defeat, both Senko no Ronde's, Mamoru-Kun Curse, and their latest title Kokuga. Comes G.Rev's Strania - The Stella Machina - (Seisou Kouki Strania/星霜鋼機ストラニア), their first title on Steam.
Previously developed for XBLA and the Nesica-(X)-Live Arcade, Strania is a shoot-em-up/shmup/STG, in which you're fighting a war against both the Stranian and the Vower armies vaying conquest. Yes, there is a story on both sides if you  check the "How-To-Play" section after you see the mechanics of the game.
Gameplay wise, the mechanics feel similar to Einhander in a sense, where you can switch weapons (up to 3) for the right situations (though there can be times where you might end up in the wrong situation if you pick the wrong weapons.) There are a total of 9 different weapons you can use in the entire game to suit your preferences (you can also level them up if you pick the same weapon again, though the colors will vary by the sides which weapons you can only upgrade to Lv.2), although...
Scoring however, requires you to use the weapons (all 9 of them in one playthough) strategically and tactically. The game uses the JP ranking system (Kyu = Dan) to score points, use them often when destroying enemies will yield bonus points (from 10kyu to 1kyu, and then from 1Dan to 10Dan), getting all 9 weapons to 1dan or higher at the end will give you a 9Mil. point bonus if you know the game in and out. Not only that, you can use the O/D system to temporary be invulnerable for a while, and have a multiplier going from X1.1 to X2.0, use when necessary.
As it is with ports that come from the Arcade/Console versions and bringing them out to Steam, this is more or less the same as the 360 port and everything is just right with it, no issues on my end, just smooth gameplay from here on in.
Lastly on the +/- sides!
+Same as it is on both XBLA/Nesica, good gameplay/mechanics/etc. (Includes both the base game and  Side: Vower!  Based on the 1.1 XBLA updated version.)
+Various options you can set your experience to the PC port. Although the - only to some users as usual with PC users, there will be problems, but nothing much updates/patches could fix. And help on the game forums if necessary.
-Unfortunately, online co-op is not in the Steam version, even though the XBLA release had it, and the co-op for that had no lag whatsoever, just smooth gameplay there too. Luckily there's Local Co-Op at least. I just hope G.Rev can find a way to add this to the Steam version if they can do it.
And to finish it off, Strania is a great game overall, the game can be tailored to your liking either for relaxed or hardcore play. I just hope this ends up being a success somehow that G.Rev can port their back catalog onto Steam. Maybe even new titles if they can! X3

Gonna jump deep into this game soon, but I just wanted to give my initial impression.
+The extra "Side Vower" content gives the game both sides of the story. Two paths with multiple difficulty options will mean more replayability than other games in the genre. Yay.
+Graphics are also a welcome step up. Some of the background elements can really pop out and surprise you. The environment really feels like part of the action.
+Weapon system is easy to get the hang of, and you can make some useful combinations, but I also really like the typical method of upgrading your shot little by little throughout the game. I give it a plus for straying from the norm while still being fun.
+Local Multiplayer yay (Not that I have friends who play these games anyway)
-My DS3 controller is only partially supported, and some buttons cannot be used. This isn't an issue with other games.
-I noticed some screen tearing while playing with native resolution (1920x1080) and there are no graphics options besides changing resolution and playing windowed/fullscreen. You may want to try configuring it in your GPU control panel. Also, there is no significant advantage compared to a lower resolution like 1280x720. The visuals don't look as sharp as they should for 1080p.
I recommend it because it makes this genre more exciting. The environment engages you, especially once you start heading into the sky and beyond. The shooting and moving mechanics are fluid, and the game is challenging without being Touhou levels of difficult. Thanks to G.rev for bringing this to Steam.

I bought this game a couple years ago and finally downloaded it this summer. The single player campaign is the kind of quality that you would expect from Rockstar - well developed and diverse characters, attention to detail, and breadth of content. I would recommend the single player of this game to anyone.
The online multiplayer, however, is such a gigantic dumpster fire that it's not even worth trying to play at this point in it's lifespan. IF YOU ARE A NEW PLAYER, DO NOT PLAY ONLINE.
There is no attempt by Rockstar to balance the gameplay whatsoever. Older players have such a large advantage over new players in almost every facet of the game - money, access to weapons, access to vehicles, activities, gameplay bonuses, etc -  that new players have little chance to play the game the way they want to. I'm fine with having some PVP, but I'm tired of being blown up by a f***ing flying motorcycle with rockets and having no way to combat it. Higher level players get health bonuses; meaning they take much, much more damage from your low level guns while you get one-shot from a high level gun. Even in game modes (expecially adversary), Rockstar stacks the bonuses and odds in favor of the team who is doing well, making harder for the losing player(s) to come back.
It's now harder for new players to grind money since Rockstar has all but eliminated solo missions and activities. Established players built their wealth on these such missions, but new players are forced to find and make lobbies with usually 4+ players to earn any sort of real income... and it's nearly impossible to find people to play with. It sometimes takes 15 minutes to fill a lobby, and that's if no one loses patience and leaves early (which many people do). Not having friends with this game makes it monumentally harder and less fun. The VIP, CEO, MC, and gunrunning mechanics are cool additions, but again, there is a high barrier to entry (buying the properties to start these endeavors are sometimes $10 million) and there's no way for new players to earn that kind of money in a reasonable amount of time. I can't play this game too often, but I would need to in order to gain the wealth needed to buy in to the fun parts of this game.
Rockstar has done a good job releasing free DLC and not charging ridiculous amounts of real money for new content like other dev companies do. That being said, the new content is turning the game in a first person shooter/war simulator instead of the crime game it should be. Fighter jets? Tanks? APCs? Military helicopters? Having these things in the game is fine in moderation, but the entire online game is SATURATED with it. Even then, the controls of GTA V is NOT suited for a FPS at all - movement is erratic, aiming is sometimes difficult, and the flight controls on keyboard literally require 3 hands. As I said earlier, new players have zero access to these - allowing established players to dominate any freemode activities. The DLCs are turning the game into a caricature of itself, and I'd rather play Saints Row for that.
All in all, the idea of online multiplayer is enticing, and perhaps earlier in it's lifespan it was playable. But the way it is now, in mid-2017, Rockstar has abandoned it's newer audience in favor of established players. Having to grind out and work your way to the top is what makes gaming fun, but in GTA V that mountian you have to climb is unreasonably and nearly impossibly steep. If you have the time and patience to commit to grinding, then go ahead. But at nearly 50 hours into online, I'm not at all close to getting into the meat of the game.

Bases can be captured from the enemy and claimed for friendly factions, creating new fast travel points and opening up missions to rescue scientists, hunt wildlife, and more.  Certain achievements will unlock new mods for your weapons in the stores.  A few collectibles in case you're really into hunting around for hidden goodies. The art style and graphic effects are pleasing.  The visuals and audio suit each other perfectly.  I didn't mess around too much with the fancy takedowns or other moves but they are cool to see. I completed a stealth/non-lethal run of DX:MD and thoroughly enjoyed it. There were plenty of alternative routes to avoid enemies and sneakily take them out. Well-designed levels, enemy positions, and questlines. Story was pretty good - made sense for the most part. Only problem is perhaps less "choice" in terms of end-game, but I think this is because they want to avoid another multi-ending option like that in DX:HR that feels janky when the player's choice isn't really honored in sequels.
I played on a 1060 3GB and 3570K, both overclocked and was able to maintain 60fps at high/very high for most of the game. Loading times were very slow on HD, so I transfered the game to my SSD and it loaded very quickly. Definitely a game that needs to be played on an SSD. Overall performance of the game was very decent with a modern GPU. It looked beautiful as well.
The length of the game is around ~20h while doing almost all the side quests. 14h for just main storyline, which isn't really that bad considering DX:HR was around 20h. If there was anything to really fault the game it's perhaps the main story could have been slightly longer. The amount of side quest content was appropriate.
Overall, hacking has improved tremendously. It's no longer a snoozefest. Praxis point spending is a lot more balanced and the new augmentations make the game more interesting. The cover system is actually useful especially with stealth takedowns. I thoroughly enjoyed the new and improved mechanics. Characters were believable for the most part, although some were definitely a bit much. There could have been a bit more follow-up with the characters you meet earlier on in the game. Would have added a touch of realism to the game.

If you want to spend hours feeling frustrated, GTAO is the game for you. Never have I wanted to enjoy a game so much yet could not because of the sheer "maldesign" of it. Glitchy, buggy, cumbersome, full of modders, and to top it all off, Rockstar Games leaves MUCH to be desired when it comes to gaming support. Something goes wrong in the game and you need help? Forget it. You get a robo "copy and paste" automated response from them. "Pester" them too much and they block you from their support page. Game-wise, loading screens can sometimes last up to 5 minutes or will just lag out entirely and drop you back into single player. Glitches/bugs never get fixed in a timely manner. Everything in the game is insanely expensive and it takes forever to make money (their way of trying to force you to buy in-game currency with real life funds). Also, due to poor design, there is no way to keep modders at bay so it is highly likely that hours upon hours of your time making money in the game will be ruined by someone with a simple mod menu. Every day in public sessions I encounter modders and they make it impossible to get anything done. Most recently, Rockstar has conducted a  "money sweep", removing funds from peoples' accounts for no reason--even those who have never received modded money or did but already had the modded money removed in previous sweeps. Some people have had millions upon millions of dollars legitimately garnered through thousands of hours of gameplay taken away by Rockstar. Others yet have had in-game money they bought with real-life currency wiped as well. As of yet, Rockstar has offered no real explanation or given any of the funds back. At the very least, GTAO should be boycotted but I'm in agreement with the people who are saying that Rockstar Games should be reported to the BBB. Until they design a better online game and take some lessons from other major MMO's support teams, I'm laying low on this game and sticking to a game that provides a more all-around rewarding experience.

I was a huge fan of the first Torchlight, but unfortunately this one was a major disappointment.
The story and the settings quite directly rip off Diablo 2, but with much less meaty goodness. Grassy foothills >> arabic desert >> swampy forest >> hellish lavaland, all while following the destructive wake of last game's hero turned evil. The repetitiveness of the quests is unreal. And it is seriously unpolished; the cinematics are literally Flash animations with hand-sketched art. I think they may have actually been production storyboards that were never finished.
They did add alot of time-saving features, but those are outweighed by too many artificial-feeling restrictions; for example, your town portal functions as a persistent Diablo 2 waygate. But when you try to open it, get ready for your character to inexplicably say "I can't do that here" (spoken by a different voice actor?!) in many crucial areas.
The gear and skill restrictions are the most infuriating. The vast majority of loot drops will either be useless or restricted to a different character class. Gems can't be upgraded, and can't be socketed into lower-level items. Most skills require a particular type of weapon equipped which heavily limits creativity in skill choices. Want to max out a basic skill early and get that Tier 3 benefit? Too bad. Each skill point has a level requirement that forces you to pick about 7 skills and level them evenly. And you'll only get them to halfway by the end of your first playthrough.
Now who wants to use the ripoff of Diablo 3's Rifts, or do a New Game Plus? Sry, nope.

I bought this game a couple years ago and finally downloaded it this summer. The single player campaign is the kind of quality that you would expect from Rockstar - well developed and diverse characters, attention to detail, and breadth of content. I would recommend the single player of this game to anyone.
The online multiplayer, however, is such a gigantic dumpster fire that it's not even worth trying to play at this point in it's lifespan. IF YOU ARE A NEW PLAYER, DO NOT PLAY ONLINE.
There is no attempt by Rockstar to balance the gameplay whatsoever. Older players have such a large advantage over new players in almost every facet of the game - money, access to weapons, access to vehicles, activities, gameplay bonuses, etc -  that new players have little chance to play the game the way they want to. I'm fine with having some PVP, but I'm tired of being blown up by a f***ing flying motorcycle with rockets and having no way to combat it. Higher level players get health bonuses; meaning they take much, much more damage from your low level guns while you get one-shot from a high level gun. Even in game modes (expecially adversary), Rockstar stacks the bonuses and odds in favor of the team who is doing well, making harder for the losing player(s) to come back.
It's now harder for new players to grind money since Rockstar has all but eliminated solo missions and activities. Established players built their wealth on these such missions, but new players are forced to find and make lobbies with usually 4+ players to earn any sort of real income... and it's nearly impossible to find people to play with. It sometimes takes 15 minutes to fill a lobby, and that's if no one loses patience and leaves early (which many people do). Not having friends with this game makes it monumentally harder and less fun. The VIP, CEO, MC, and gunrunning mechanics are cool additions, but again, there is a high barrier to entry (buying the properties to start these endeavors are sometimes $10 million) and there's no way for new players to earn that kind of money in a reasonable amount of time. I can't play this game too often, but I would need to in order to gain the wealth needed to buy in to the fun parts of this game.
Rockstar has done a good job releasing free DLC and not charging ridiculous amounts of real money for new content like other dev companies do. That being said, the new content is turning the game in a first person shooter/war simulator instead of the crime game it should be. Fighter jets? Tanks? APCs? Military helicopters? Having these things in the game is fine in moderation, but the entire online game is SATURATED with it. Even then, the controls of GTA V is NOT suited for a FPS at all - movement is erratic, aiming is sometimes difficult, and the flight controls on keyboard literally require 3 hands. As I said earlier, new players have zero access to these - allowing established players to dominate any freemode activities. The DLCs are turning the game into a caricature of itself, and I'd rather play Saints Row for that.
All in all, the idea of online multiplayer is enticing, and perhaps earlier in it's lifespan it was playable. But the way it is now, in mid-2017, Rockstar has abandoned it's newer audience in favor of established players. Having to grind out and work your way to the top is what makes gaming fun, but in GTA V that mountian you have to climb is unreasonably and nearly impossibly steep. If you have the time and patience to commit to grinding, then go ahead. But at nearly 50 hours into online, I'm not at all close to getting into the meat of the game.

First of all, this is an Early Access review, so my conclusion may change after release!
But today I have to say that I can not recommend the Game as it is.
To summarize the game: you will meet different girls along your way and you are encouraged to let everyone fall in love with you, using gifts, dates and personality. Earn money, improve your hobbies, get better jobs and idle.
My motivation to play that game is a mixture of interests in self-made games, the Unity 3D Engine and Cookie-Clicker (Stream Tag-search brought me here). The additional 'Free-to-play' is the cherry on the cake. And to be honest, the game has many pros:
- it looks and feels like homemade with loving designed Images
- it's done by a small group of three people
- it's free to play
But on the other hand there are so many points that are bugging me, like:
- why takes it longer to get the max-level at a job after I reseted the game for a sufficient higher 'Prestige Boost'?
- why is there the need of n hearts (you can get them by clicking on the girls) when the gifts the girls want surmount the needed number by far?
- the girls feel highly replaceable and without any personality..
- ...

And beside some bigger or smaller issues, my biggest problem: the game is no fun. All I can do is idle. I'm sitting here and wait three more days to get my 'tenderness' to level 32, just to get into the next stage of waiting days without getting any motivation. All-in-all it feels like the whole game has a lack of  motivate people to play, idle or even spent money. Because I could by timesteps and other nice little helper to achieve my goal way faster, but what for and what is the goal?
My only personal impulsion is, to anatomize different types of games and how the in-game economy will change.
The next updates will bring us a more clearer vision of the final game, but I can't imagine that there will be wide changes. If you watch the youtube-channel of  Sad Panda Studios, you will fall over the video about patreon and the next ideas the devs have [there are evidence of full-body images, other settings and environments, a nude mod]  – but I'm not sure if any idea will ever be in the game.

I remember the first time that my mom accidently bought me Ultimate Mortal Kombat 3 for SNES. I was so very young and impressionable. Many fond memories...Once I even uppercutted a girl in the first grade while trying to show her my moves...She later became my girlfriend..
Anyway, so Mortal Kombat X; I'm pretty impressed. Overall I like it a lot, and it reminds me more of the older games than ever.
- Story mode is fun and decently written.
- Fighting feels fluid and if you're using a controller the response time is smooth.
- Nice fatalities as always. They are less difficult to perform  (there is even an 'easy fatality' perk you can use, not that you really need them.)
- 'The Krypt' is kind of a neat feature. You explore a few areas to unlock different items and extras in the game (i.e. Character fatalities + brutalities, Concept Art, Music, etc.)
- Various kinds of tower fights keep the towers interesting. Klassic Towers, Living Towers, and other kinds of Challenge Towers.
- Faction wars are introduced here, you join a faction and pull off a certain amount of challenges to bring your faction to the #1 spot. The #1 faction is awarded stuff.
- Use the scenery in the level to beat your opponent to trash (pick up and throw things, bash their heads into stuff, etc.)
- Use the scenery all of the different levels; throw some stuff, swing from some vines, and get yourself unstuck from the corners. Very cool addition to make levels come alive.
- The cutscene button fighting in story mode is odd and pointless. It effects nothing except to spice up some of the cutscenes and keep the player interested i suppose.
- Online has a few issues, I've read various complaints but haven't played much online to be honest. I try to do my bit in the faction wars. One thing is the connection cuts in and out for some reason.
- MKX lacks some of the best characters you would want to play. You might even see them in story mode. I feel like that let me down. No spoilers here, but there are some characters you can even fight against that you can't play as.
- The DLC model is just not what Mortal Kombat once was. You used to be able to unlock characters and now you just pay for them. But hey, I guess it is what it is. The DLC packs are alright. Also, what's the point of putting in the Krypt if you can pay $20 to unlock everything??
This Mortal Kombat really brings the pain!!! As a huge fan of the series, I can finally honestly say that there's a new(er) MK that I truely love. It feels like an old MK, but with beautiful graphics, and a decent ongoing story line to boot. The story mode is pretty fun and continues the lore of MK in a fairly interesting way. While some of the classic older characters are present, some fan favorites are missing. It doesn't help that you fight/see some of them in the story mode!
Online is pretty fun, but it feels like it could be executed better and hopefully will be in the future. In fact it occasionally cuts out on me :[.
There are also a few extra features such as the Krypt and Faction Wars that are interesting aspects of the game. Several kinds of towers and faction challenges keep the game fairly interesting.
- Definately buy on sale, if you're a fan of the series or at least of MK9, you'll definately like this one. It certainly does it for me! DLC can be as frusterating as ever. Find a bundle if possible.

I really like this game. But in no way do I love this game. There are many reasons why, and I would love to keep this review to being short and sweet.
PROS:
- I love the weapon and armour system in this game. The random piece of armour or random weapon that you get really adds to the "Rogue-Lite" feeling of this game.
- The vast amount of levels. Playing this game has never ceased for me to find something new that I have either; stumbled upon by complete accident or spent minutes grinding.
- The range of enemies. The amount of enemies in this game is actually friggin' jaw-dropping. I always fall upon a whole new, sometimes hardcore, enemy. This makes the game seem like it could be played forever due to the fact that there's always something new.
- The Daily Challenges. The fact that this game gets new dailies... Daily, is amazing. The way that you can play the game every day and get a whole new run that everyone else would be doing. This also adds to the whole "Rogue-Lite" feeling.
- The pets!! I, myself, am an avid animal lover. The fact that you can get animals in this game to fight alongside you and to kill your wildest foes is beyond happiness for me. I love picking out my cute, sometimes horrifying, pet.
Cons:
- The biggest problem I see with this game is how GRINDY it feels. Okay, sure, that's to be expected of a "Rogue-Lite" but in no way should it be as grindy as it is. I find myself constantly trying to get that whole new weapon that I need or the final piece of armour that I need to complete my collection. Apart from the grinding, there's really nothing else I can flaw about this game. Sure, the actual gameplay gets some getting used to, and the fact that some of the missions seem very repetative, this game is really good.
I would really recommend this game if you're on the hunt for that new Rogue-Lite to keep you on your toes for a few hours or maybe days. Solid game with solid elements and solid gameplay. I must-buy for you avid Rogue-Lite fans.

Shattered Planet is a very well made Sci-Fi Rogue-Like.  The story is interesting, and the concept of playing as a series of clones, sent to your sure death in the name of Science and Exploration, is pretty great.  As a warning - this does mean perma-death, for those who don't like the mechanic.  There are a few different ways to play the game (including a daily challenge-type mode) and none of it feels unpolished.   There are loads of unlockables, as well as several environmental and enemy types that have varying interactions.  I had a lot of fun discovering all the crazy, deadly and bizzarely adorable content in this game.
This game really is lacking in very few areas.  It does rely more heavily on RNG than any Rogue-Like I've ever played.  The difficulty (for me) eventually ramped up so hard that I couldn't begin to finish the game.  I have a suspicion that playing with one of the unlockable characters might have helped, but the idea of re-raising all of your stats (which carry over from clone to clone) turned me off.  I had spent way too much time just upgrading the one character I had started with.  As much as I enjoyed the game, I couldn't see playing through everything I'd already done all over again, just to get a chance to finish the content I had remaining.
Still worth the price, and a fun way to spend some hours.  Give 'er a go.  I also found out that Shattered Planet is available on mobile.  As a turn-based game, with such depth, I actually would have prefered having it for my tablet.  For no particular reason, other than because there are so few games like this on mobile that are worth a damn.

So I've played quite a bit of Shattered Planet, so I thought I'd give my thoughts. I've taken the Mercenary class up to level 60, and almost got all the items and things. For anyone that likes a simple, elegant game that you don't have to pump hours and hours into to play, then this is something you should try. Nice class system, beautiful landscapes and wonderful creature designs too. At first I thought that the small range of world types and short levels would become tiring, but because they are procedurally generated the awe of discovery is always there. I love that the mystery fluids are randomised each time, because you have to develop efficient and safe ways of trying them, or take the risk of using them blind! Having the daily challenge feature is AWESOME in my opinion, as it gives you a reason to come back every day, which then sets you off for another 45 minutes of fun. I wouldn't recommend playing this game LOTS as the set pieces and quests begin to lose their value, but play a little bit each day and you'll find yourself looking forward to the next daily challenge, the next quest! A few small gripes however, I wish there was a way to naturally increase fate that stays between adventures, as it is a little annoying to have a super powerful, 60 strength Mercenary fail an objective as I only have 5 fate :/ ah well. Even if it was suuuper expensive or something like that, it'd be worth it! I also think it would be cool to have some feature where you could quest for particualr weapons/items/encounters that you don't have somehow, as simply farming ROSA gets reeeeal old, especially when you don't know what quality weapon you are after.
tl;dr
GAMEPLAY: 8.5/10
REPLAYABILITY: 7.5/10- add in those weapon quests, and you've got yourself a 10 :)
ART STYLE 10/10- just lovely to look at!
STORY: 4/10- the blight is mysterious, and could be delved deeper into. It's not currently a game to play for story (in my opinion)
OVERALL ENJOYMENT: 8/10
OVERALL REMARK: if you're looking for a lite relief between story-heavy RPGs, give this little number a go. It's a breath of fresh air that changes every day!

The game has a goofy storyline which is not really interesting, but I guess that's to be expected when the game should be played for ten to fifteen minutes. What stopped me from giving this game a dislike is how nice the island looked. The people, however, seemed very static. I recall only one person moving, and there were only four people you can talk with.

You play as a tourist who got 10% off his vacation to the most beautiful island that ever existed.  You begin this epic vacation adventure on the beach and soon realize that all you want and need to satisfy your every desire is a hot dog.  You race to the hot dog stand as fast as your wide torso can waddle only to find that you have no money to buy the hot dog of your dreams.  The friendly hot dog salesman helps you by sending you to the local ice cream shop to earn some money.  You explore the town to find the ice cream shop but can't take too long because your calorie counter is quickly depleting.  You get to the ice cream shop.  He says he needs coconuts and will pay for 5 coconuts.  He gives you a coconut collecting device and sends you back to the beach to collect the mucho importante coconuts.  You mosey on to the beach and begin scooping up coconuts but better watch out for those pesky crabs.  After getting the 5 coconuts you run back to the ice cream shop.  He pays you for delivering the goods and tells you to go to Diego's Pizza if you want to earn more cash.  You dash over to see Diego and he desperately needs a pineapple to make pineapple pizza for the hungry tourists so he sends you into the nearby jungle to meet the pineapple man.  When you get to the pineapple man he quickly proclaims that he never gives pineapples for free but if you find his lost parrot he will reward you with a pineapple.  You must find this parrot so you run around the jungle to catch the parrot who does not want to be caught.  You finally catch the evasive bird and return him to the pineapple man who kindly pays you the bird bounty.  You take the pineapple and rush it back to Diego the pizza man.  He happily pays you for your trouble and now you have the $3.50 you need to go and buy the hot dog you are salivating for. If you have played and enjoyed the gameplay mechanics of Far Cry 3, then you will most likely enjoy this title. FC3: Blood Dragon has essentially the same gameplay mechanics of Far Cry 3, without some of the more in-depth extras such as crafting and the level-up talent selection (tattos). A preset talent is given at each level instead of giving the player a choice. Aside from the main story missions, there are garrison liberations, collectibles and side missions. Liberating a garrison will unlock 1 or 2 side missions. Completing a side mission will unlock a purchasable weapon upgrade. Certain upgrades are unlocked by getting collectibles. Once certain garrisons are liberated maps with the location of all collectibles become available for purchase. All enemies drop money.
The story and setting parody a generic 1980s action movie set in a dystopic-future where cyborgs and neon are commonplace. It reminded of a mixture of "Escape from New York", "Total Recall" and "Universal Soldier". The voice acting and dialog is about as good as I would expect from a 1980s action movie, so I asumed that this was on purpose. The story is short. I think there were about 12 story missions total. I was able to complete the story and side missions and get all of the collectibles in about 16 hours.
The game world is aesthetically pleasing in my opinion. The lighting, however, is always a very dark red. This was a bit annoying for me as there is also a lot of bright neon, especially on the bow. I found that this contrast in lighting fatigued my eyes after a few hours. The cutscenes are all done in a pixel-art animation/slideshow with voice acting that was reminiscent of any number of video games in the late 1980s. I found this to be somewhat charming, but I would much rather have had cutscenes that were rendered using the game engine.
Overall, I enjoyed my time with this title. I thought the story was funny and ended well, and I liked the gameplay mechanics. In retrospect, I should have finished the main story before doing any of the extra content so that I would have had more time to utilize the reward that is given to the player.

Play with all the best Far Cry 3 perks without having to level up to use them. Blood Dragon is a bottled up version of Far Cry 3's great gameplay culminated in a cheesy 1980s style bad boy storyline. Sneaking around is so 21st century--run and gun your way to badass stardom!

This is going to be tough to recommend this game. I dont want to give it a "thumbs down" because the game is usually on sale or at least offered at a reduced price. So, my only recommendation is really based on purchasing the game for equal or less than what I paid for the game. That price was $11.99
What can go wrong? Far Cry 3: great map, solid game play, good AI, great environment, the whole nine yards. So, if the developers mod the game, reskin it, give it post 80's futuristic feel, add neon dinosaurs, and you should have a winner. But sadly, its immediately apparent that everyone involved took everything too far and everything was overdone. Its almost as if they used a overkill policy just to make sure they didnt miss their mark. If the goal was to create a nostalgic retro futuristic shooter off the FC3 platform they not only hit that target but they actually nuked it.
The redeeming qualities of this game are all of the same qualities in Far Cry 3. All of the gun play and melee are the same. The map is the same. The animals are basically the same (except a few large T-Rexes).
Im not going to get into to explaining the story line or the main character too much. Its not important. You have one bionic arm and your guy flips people off, has reload animations that are 80's ridiculous, and the jokes and comments will make you smirk for the first 5 mins before becoming very annoying. Your standard bad guys have digital sounding voices that also get very annoying after a few minutes. But as in FC3, those bad guys also said much of the same things too and were almost as annoying. I think the beautiful environment in FC3 distracted me enough to not have to pay too much attention to what the bad guys were saying. But in FC3-Blood Dragon, the whole world is dark and the excessive neon doesnt distract. Matter of fact, your brain starts to block it out after a few minutes and then youre left in this permanently dark world.
So, it sounds like I hate the game, right? Well, kinda-sorta. But not really. All of the preview videos are fair. They show you exactly what you are getting; bad jokes, dark environment with neon, robots, and neon 1/2 robot dinosaurs. I purchased the game after finishing FC3. I wanted to continue playing the game and I did not want to actually replay the same story. So I got exactly what the previews showed me. However...
I only played the game for about 1.5-2 hours before getting bored with it. At that point, I bought Far Cry 2 and enjoyed that immensely. So, if youre like me and finished Far Cry 3 and are still craving a Far Cry adventure, get FC2 if you havent played it yet...its great. But if you want neon dinosaurs then Blood Dragon is for you. It is worth the 11.99 USD that I paid for it, I dont regret that. And I feel like I got my money's worth. So at that price or less and this is a safe buy. Even if you only get 2 hrs out of it like I did, its the same amount of $ to go see a 2 hr movie. Dollars to Donuts

As far as DLC for a game goes, this exactly what it should be. The length is perfect for the money, and if you find it on sale you can get it pretty cheap. The graphics and the gameplay are very similar to Far Cry 3, but with a few notable exceptions (like the red tint and how you feel way more powerful than Jason Brody). Check this game out, you'll have probably have a great time, unless you got a stick up your butt.

Wow, this game feels awful.
I watched some video tutorials because the game has absolutely no kind of in-game tutorial or guidance. The combos in this game are really short and loose.
The animations are barely animations; going in and out of an attac is like pressing back and forward in a PowerPoint. No clever use of squash and stretch tweening or anything.
The hitboxes are often VERY unclear without seeing them in the training mode. Many of them, considering how SMALL a screen real-estate each character takes up, are oddly displaced or truncated and often smaller/shorter than the weapon sprite, even when they have outrageous sweeps of wind-like SFX trailing them. If a weapon tries to give off an "animation" to show a sweeping motion, it really just places and hangs a hitbox at the end of the weapon. Why? I don't know.
This game is smash-like. However, its control differences are... awkward. Basically, there's no up weak attack (an up A) in the air, but you DO have an up heavy attack (an up-B) in the air. Did the game just forget to make an up air weak attack? It FEELS like there are moves missing. Why would they just... make that arbitrary, confusing change to such a simple idea as "press a different direction with a button to make different attacks"? Some directions just share an attack and I can't think of the logic behind it.
Jumps are also slow, syruppy, and weightless. Fast falling is slow across the board. It feels like I'm playing a death match on an air hockey table.
Maybe this game has more going for it when you learn more about it, but it fails to even feel good in my hands so... why would I give it more time?
The character designs are better than they appear from a distance, but you're always viewing them from a distance. From that distance, they look muddled and indinstinct. Few characters have a strong enough silhouette to differentiate them from the distance they're most often seen. I don't know WHY this game hasn't changed its character design methodolody with recent characters. They're all heavily ornamented chibi heads on very, very similar bodytypes. This ISN'T good art direction for the camera system.
This isn't just a flaw in the art but in the design of the game; "where the hell am I?" is a question I asked myself too often in my head.
I regret spending any amount of time with it.

Just finished the game for the first time right before writing this, and I have to say, it's an amazing game, despite the add-ons that Square Enix have been pushing for it that I couldn't afford. Very compelling story, convincing characters/plotlines, and a properly immersive world.
In my first playthrough, I wanted to get the full depth of the lore that the game had to offer, and I was not disappointed. Lots of optional reading material and plenty of people to talk to get into what's happening in the world. I'm pretty sure I got to everything on my playthrough (if not, then I missed
little), and I truly feel it was well worth the money. Thing is, all of that is optional - the game has a lot to offer in the way of lore, but only meets you halfway. To get the rest, you gotta take the time to explore it, because it won't give it to you otherwise. Whether that would be is worth the money to you is your choice, but I consider it money well spent in my case.
And to anyone who cares, I would say that HR was a better game overall, but MD follows it well.
All that being said...it has a few bugs. There were times where my game would crash during a loading screen, which was annoying but not too much so, since it always autosaved at very convenient times.
There were also a few glitches every here and there, but none of them were gamebreakers.
Ultimately, I
recommend this game to those who love a good story, especially so if you're into sci-fantasy and/or cyberpunk genres. Even if you're not into that stuff, the toys this game lets you play with are a ton of fun to mess around with. Thumbs up to the developers!

To sum it up, this was an amazing 10/10 game that was cut far too short, leaving it with a 5/10 rating.
