Can't even render the tank, but you know where it is because you magically die at the spawn every 10 seconds from a shell.
What started as a favorite of mine has been left on the way side because devs apparently don't play it to see what's broken. Used to be realistic, used to be fun, used to play it every day.
2nd Iteration of the Review:
UPGRADE: I have recently upgraded to a GTX1050TI OC and an SSD. Everything is much less clunky and I have found the graphics and physics to be very good.
MINOR CHANGE: The tanks are still an issue, but out of about 10 matches I've played in the past 48 hours, I have only had tank trolls once. Several changes were made that make the playing field levelled against tanks a little. That being said, I still had to simply quit 2 matches because there was no point in trying.
POSITIVE CHANGE:
I just began a new character and within 24 hours had the entry level weapon levelled up to the max and had outfitted my character with full anti-tank gear. The grinding required has been reduced dramatically from what I can see. This is a very positive change!
POSITIVE CHANGE:
I am earning credits and able to purchase the above upgrades much faster. Big benefit! The new credit system is unique and I think it works very well.
FOR ALL NEW PLAYERS:
Get on youtube and look up some videos on how to survive this game, there are videos that walk through tank hunting, sniping, capping CPs, etc. This will help your rid you of a lot of frustration!
I am upgrading this to recommended again. I believe they have addressed enough issues to satisfy my expectations for a free-to-play game.

I played Diablo II way back in the day, so this was a nice nostalgia trip. Many people are calling this better than Diablo. I agree. But while it perfects everything Diablo gets wrong it's still highly repetitive and not fulfilling.
I beat this game on Normal with Engineer class. I increased my 'strength' stat and I hammered through levels with mainly one special and the occasional foot stomp. Enemies aren't that difficult to defeat until the last stage. The story is very bland. In most games I generally listen to every NPC talk, yet every mission is to either kill or retrieve. Loot isn't that fulfilling since once you get one cool weapon or armor, you'll be upgrading it within five minutes for the next one. You never feel like your character is progressing or becoming a badass.
On the positives I enjoyed the colorful cartoony style. While the loot is ultimately not fulfilling, it's quite bountiful and rewarding in that slot machine type of way. If you like to click stuff, this can get quite addictive. I did find some enjoyment in hammering the crowded dungeons. The addition of the pet is awesome except the pet NEVER dies! Sending the pet home to sell stuff is genius. There needs to be more complexity added to the pet. Torchlight II isn't challenging, rewarding, or interesting. I'd only recommend if doing co-op.

After having completed the initial Trine game, it was an obvious step to purchase Trine 2 as well. And also obvious that nothing but Complete Story would suffice,  which boasts a good amount of extra levels and skills to complete puzzles with as well.
It goes without saying that Trine 2 was just as enjoyable, if not moreso, than the first Trine. New ways to complete puzzles or battle foes were added. It's the perfect co-op game for three people: easy to learn, fun to master and you'll have a great time whether you're failing spectaculary trying to work together or beating the game together.
One notorious change to the first Trine instalment is that Trine 2 boasts far more difficult challenges in the form of difficulty and achievements. While the first Trine was easy to beat and complete with all achievements and 100% completion under 10 hours, there's a far broader amount of achievements, and thus challenges, in Trine 2.
For a battle-hardened single player gaming veteran, you'll breeze right through it, although you might be slightly annoyed trying to get all the achievements and experience. Just like the first Trine, and undoubtly the upcoming Trine 3, Trine 2 is excellent enjoyment that only grows even more enjoyable with friends.

This game is absolutely terrible. Many people claim that it's fair and balance and that the brawlhalla devs work hard to keep it so. I strongly disagree with such a bold statement as that, this game is far from balance. Lets go over some of the reasons why this game is so unbalance.
------------------------lance-----------------------------------
This weapon is probably the most broken weapon in the game. It has a crap ton of range and can be used in some tricky ways. Personaly all I see is people consistent spamming slight then just try to smack you down with some outragious combo that you cannot even douge out of. Overall this weapon is massive toxic and I want to quit the game every time I see someone palying a legend who uses this weapon. It not only have a crap ton of range, but it does a crap ton of damage and will sned you flying off the map on higher hps (something only heavy weapons really do). Overall I think is massively unbalance, because people can go around basically spamming the crap out of the range advantage that they get on this weapon.
--------------------Katars-------------------------------------
This weapon not only is the fastest weapon in the game, it does a crap ton of damage as well and get alot of priority in attack clashes becuase it has so much range. Generally people using this weapon spam light attacks on you all game until you die, and the side light on this weapon sends you flying to your death off the map (despite the fact that it is really fast and should hit less harder). I feel that the fact taht this weapon is both fast and does a large amount of damage in the short periode of time you have to do something before they unleash a really fast string on you is pretty unbalance.
--------------------Community-------------------------------
Lets be honest here and I think most people would agree that he community on this game is♥♥♥♥♥♥ This game requires no skill if you are able to play Orion, Vraxx, or any other mega spam legend, you are on your way to daimond my friend. (Orion gets sigs that have little to almost no recovery time, pretty unbalance). This game is all about who can spam their sigs the most and who can spam their light attacks the most. There is a very small pool of legends that do not really encourage people to spam abilities. Exept the only problem is that everyone spams really spammable ranged legends, because these champions have an advantage over everyone else, Brawlhalla seems to ignore the advantages that anyone gets while playing with weapons that have high damage and high range. Granted these weapons can be slow and can be dodged, but a well timed attack while your on red hp and your instantly dead. Besides, everyone with these said weapons generally try to play extreamly passive and wait for you to come attack them, or they spam you with sig moves until you die. Overall the community is toxic, because people try to find some really non-skilled ways to beat everyone.

------------------------------Swords--------------------------------
If you want to get to daimond really easily. just play any legend with a sword. I went into 4 1v1 games to test out how unbalance the sword was and I won by just pressing side light and neutral light and down light all game. It is really unfortunate that such a weapon exist that has really fast speeds and very long range, the sword is massively spammanble, and is generally given to players who are extreamly fast. This is really unbalance, because some legends can just run around the map spamming light attacks on you all game and you can't do anything, because their range gives them priority in attack clashes. Not to mention the fact that I can throw a bomb at someone on red hp and they still live, but you get hit by the side light with this sword are your finished you are dead, because you get flung all the way off the map. Another point is the easiest true combo in the game to pull off.
------------------------Overall Opinion----------------------------
Sense the day that I have started on this game I have had gained nothing from it. I have no fun, becuase of the toxic community, I get no value from this game. I generally leave this game feeling disatisfied and extreamly frustrated from getting spammed by a player using something that I have a hard time playing against. I have decided to delete this game as I have no further point in playing such a broken, unbalance, peice of crap. If you are looking for a game to play with your friends, this game might be fun, but if you play competitive ranked, this game is going to kick your♥♥♥♥♥and every single day you will slowly hate this game more and more until you see no value in it.
-------------------------------------Playing passive-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
If you ever want to win any game you just play passive. The creators of brawlhalla benefit passive players over aggresive players. Despite the fact that brawlhalla makes players that are built to play aggresive, for example, wu shang. Reasons why passive players can win in a sense is that they have to play the game solely on reacting to the enemies attack. Having the second attack you have more of an advantage and are able to easily punished miss timmed attacks on you. The other fact that helps in passive play is chain dodging as it allows you to use multiple dodges to get away from your enemy. Another point I would like to add on playing passive is that its really hard to counter, if the other person is playing aggresive, sure you can use invencibility frames to get a little counter play on passive players, but this only goes so far and can easily be counters as well. Over all this game is complete cancer, and I have tried over and over, er dwonloading this game, practicing and anything I can do to make myself better, and more and more I grow a hating passion for this game. This game is a waste of your time and this game is created to make your rage and almost punch your fist through your monitor screen.

It's a relatively short game, and as seen by my time played I would like to note I didn't get all the achievements but I wasn't really trying.
As a game I would say it's an on rails puzzle game. The path is quite linear. Regarding puzzles they don't give you a pop up telling you exactly how to play it so it requires some figuring out but they're intersting...interesting in that they aren't hard but intersting in how the boys solve the problem they face in their world.
A major strength of the game is the lack of dialogue as we are used for story based or really...any games. Despite the lack of text we're so accustomed to have shoved down our throats you can feel the emotion and discussions in the game. It's amazing because it allows every person to imagine in their mind how the exact dialogue would play out between characters.
Call back to a day where you were young and watching something like "The Neverending Story"...it evokes many of the same feelings in short amount of time. Joys and laughs, gasps and sadness.
Gravely speaking, by the end of the game you'll be spun into a world of emotional webbing where ultimately the rain you see outside your home reflects the world crying alongside you.

The first thing I want to say is this, I CAN'T stop playing this game. Crush Crush is a cute non-adult version of HuniePop with minor "clicker" game aspects. I will compare this game to HuniePop a bit and some aspects of the "clicker" part of this game will be compared to the other "clicker" games I have played such as Sakura Clicker, Clicker Heroes, Epic Clicker Journey, etc...
I usually start of with the cons of the games I review but, honestly I can't think of many bad things about this game, so for this review I will be starting of with the pros.
Pros:
-The Girls. Just like HuniePop the developers did a really good job on the design and attitudes of each of this games girls. There are a total of 11 girls to woo and more to come. I like every one of this games girls, Cassie is sassy and doesn't take♥♥♥♥♥♥ Mio is sweet and kind, Quill is cute and a cat girl (win, win in my book), Elle likes to sleep a lot or has some form of narcolepsy and is "dim witted" (not the smartest but, is very likable), Iro is a bad♥♥♥♥♥that loves motorcycles, Bonnibel is a baker who seems to be older and more "experienced" with "stuff", she refers to the player as sugar and darling which is sexy, Fumi is a time traveler that is from the future and may be the only girl that has any form of nude picture of her in the game, Bearverly is a bear, Nina is a sexy house maid, Alpha is holographic Pop idol star, and Pamu is a goddess (I believe).
-Gems. Gems are a form of in-game currency either bought with real money or awarded for reaching new relationship levels with each girl. Gems can be a major way to increase the amount of stuff you can get done in a run of the game. Allowing increased time blocks allowing to do more things at once, increase over progression of jobs, hobbies and heat gaining, and time skips, moving forward jobs, hobbies, a heart requirements ahead without any actual wait.
-Game Reset. You can reset your game like most "clicker" games to decrease the amount of time it takes for thing to progress in-game.
-Look/Overall Feel. I love the overlay of this game the colors fit well and the graphic style cute and really nice.
-Jobs/Way To Make Money. There many jobs you can work at to increase the amount of in-game cash you have.You can also work as many jobs as you can as long as you have to the time blocks to do so.
-Price Of Game/Gems. The game itself is completely free and the prices for this games special in-game currency Gems is well set. $1 (US) will get you 10 diamonds which a great deal especially since how useful diamonds can be. You have other options as well that give a larger "percent bonus" of extra gems with each next level.
-Dialogue. I love the way the girls act and talk in this game. From sassy insults to cute and lovable complements this game did a very good job on the dialogue for each girl.
-Save/Load Games. Yeah that's right you can save and load games! Currently you have 2 save slots for games and you can load each them anytime you want and no matter which game you last loaded both will progress while in or out of the game. There is also loadable auto save slot that will be coming some time soon!
Cons:
-Wait Time. Some times hobbies just take way to long to increase in level at this present moment in my game, most if not all my hobbies require days to increase once with a almost 30 times multiplier.
-In Game Currency. The in-game currency isn't enough. The jobs are cool but, they give too little money for the time blocks they require there should be more ways to earn money or the jobs should give more of the bat. This would be a good way to have more "clicker" sections to the game because of right now this game shouldn't tagged as one.
-The Girls' Requirements. Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥the requirements for the later girls/relationship levels are ridiculous and absurd. Having to have a hobby over level 30, billions and billions of dollars for gifts that are way over priced. This can remove a lot of fun from the game.
Overall this game is awesome! I would recommend this game to anyone just looking to play a fun time "passer" and I say passer instead of waster because this game is not a waist of time to play. I understand the dating sim part of the game may turn people away but, give the game a chance I promise you will not regret it!

In general I hate oldschool adventure games, with their nonsense non-logic, pixel hunting, try everything on everything, and generally broken mechanics.
This isn't one of those, instead it's a series of discrete, self-contained logic puzzles. Most players will probably have seen at least some of these puzzle types before.
The story is minimal and mostly serves as a loose way to tie the puzzles together.
I enjoyed this because if I got stuck it was because I was too dumb to logically figure it out, and not because of the reasons that generally put me off adventure games.
Flickering graphics and game crashed when i finished the final puzzle. Good if you like generic puzzle games.

Mankind Divided exhibits a definite improvement in level design and gameplay. Whilst still stealth-oriented, levels exude atmosphere with on-point art direction and contain more verticality. This works well in tandem with new powers to offer more options, pathways, and compromises. Prague, the single hub world, is dense and dynamic; hiding many chunky side quests. The sticking point for many will be the scope of the main story; while still self-contained, it’s less ambitious than the original or Human Revolution, and feels like the pilot to a longer series. Microtransactions and Breach mode have no impact on the campaign and should be ignored.

The action-movie dialog is amusing for about five minutes, and then painful for the next 2-6 hours. Likewise with the awkward slide-y shooter mechanics and cumbersome vehicle driving sections.
The things Blood Dragon gets right are the exact same things Far Cry 3 gets right. Sharks are terrifying. The world is pretty. And everyone is combustible. Other than that, every change Blood Dragon made feels like a misstep.

Was the very first question someone asked me about Trine 2 was:
And I kid you not folks, I looked at the person and tried desperately to not shout out loud "YOU DON'T KNOW TRINE 2!???" To be frank, I just calmly(I'm serious) told the person it's a 3 player co-op action/adventure/small rpg/ side scrolling platformer game in a 2.5D environment with gorgeous graphics and puzzling puzzles to test your mettle on.
The sequel to Frozenbyte's earlier title Trine, Trine 2 builds upon it's predecessor foundations and game-play by flushing it all out. By means of adding even more graphical options and making the game stand out aesthetic wise to fit the side scrolling theme. The rpg skills you earn have been expanded so you can learn more than the limited amount you can spend points on in the first game. The puzzles you thought were easy in Trine 1 are perhaps significantly harder(just a little wee bit hard, depending if you can handle the mental strain) Granted it's not intensive as puzzles as the Portal franchise from Valve. Rather the puzzles are just there to halt your progress and think about in a minute or two on how to solve it.
Story wise our three unfortunate(Or fortunate in finding trouble along the way) main protagonists find themselves entangled with a princess to save her kingdom from evil...
BORING! Would've been your first impression of it, but it's far from a simple adventure to save a kingdom. Far from it indeed. There are documents hidden in chests scattered throughout the levels to provide further back story on the game itself. Which is invaluably precious in providing insight onto the simple task assigned above by a princess. I'll leave the rest to your imagination to see how the story will unfold...
I played Trine 2 with 2 other friends of mine and had an absolute blast of a time enjoying the co-op aspect and coordinating with each other to advance to the next level. With the occasional friendly fire I accidently(sometimes) hit them with. Unintentional though! I by no means am a sadistic friend who enjoys the torment of my friends dying before me... Moving on, the options to play in co-op are a lot. you can choose to turn off friendly fire(don't turn this mode off when playing with friends to enjoy their suffering), turning off the option to lift your comrades with boxes,  or put on classic mode and stick with one character, or cheat and have the ability to choose on the fly a different character.
3 Shield-Bro's!? No problem. Let's shield our way!
3 Thieves!? Lots of swinging vines here and there...
3 Wizards!? Oh, the Box and Plank madness ensues!!!
^ Or perhaps you young adventurers want to dabble and mix and match.
2 Knights and 1 mage
2 Thieves and 1 knight
2 Mages and 1thief
Go play with the combinations and pick whichever one suit your needs.
Honestly, the game has much more appeal and replay ability if you play with a friend locally or in multiplayer, or if you're a gamer who likes playing it solo by all means do so! It depends on your play style of course. Just remember to get the most enjoyment of the experience my friend!

This game is an amazing casual experience and has a lot of depth for more hard-core players, but it suffers from circular hit boxing, and mechanics and abilities that can be abused in fairly toxic ways. Additionally, the competitive ranked ladder consists almost entirely of yours truly and other video-game addicted scumbags who just want that next elo award and will do anything to get there.
I have over 500 hours on this game and it's one of my favorite games of all time. I’ve played consistently in the competitive scene and I beat high-elo players, but I also know I can’t touch the pros despite my occasional lucky match.
If you’re looking for a fun, cartoony fighting game or just a good couch experience to enjoy between friends, this is a wonderful game, and can even be fun to play solo in the ‘tournament’ mode.

If you’re looking for a finely-tuned competitive fighting game with smooth mechanics and a huge variance in play, you’re not going to find that in Brawlhalla. However, it’s updated consistently and has a
great company behind it.
PROS:
1. Cartoony, but in a pleasing and artful way. (I like the art style at least)
2. Soundtrack is good if a bit repetitive and kinda loud.
3. Weapon sounds and animations are on-point and hitting an opponent feels good.
3. Unique and well-thought out game mechanics, if easily ‘abused’.  I.E. Dodge and invincibility frames, the parry play style, weapon throws.
4.  A passionate dev team who release updates weekly and communicate with the community consistently.
5.  Easy to play, hard to master.
6. Completely free-to-play.
CONS:
1. The online PvP and ranked ladders are fairly grind-to-win and are topped by people who have been playing for 1-2 years before open beta began, so you’re at a disadvantage the whole time.
2. The community ranges from being incredibly toxic, homophobic and mean to some very awesome, considerate people who I enjoy spending time with.
3. The game mechanics can be 'exploited' easily. As in, people can become quite high elo by just spamming ranked games and doing the same thing over and over because it works.
4. Invincibility frames give the reactive player an advantage over the proactive player.
5. Very addicting. I consistently have to uninstall this game because it takes over my life and keeps me from being healthy, but that’s kind of a ‘me problem’.
6. Taunts. I hate them.
I’ll probably play this game for many more months because of how competitive and avid of a player I am, but it’s definitely not everyone’s cup of tea, and has caused me more rage and hair-pulling then any MOBA ever could.

There is a particular segment of the gaming community whose deepest love is for hard-core simulations.  These simulations are like a blend of puzzle-game and action game, where you get as much satisfaction from learning how to use the simulated systems as from achieving goals within the game.  There is an element of education, as well, because you know that what you are learning is solidly based on how things work (or might work) in the real world, without any sugar-coating or compromises for "accessibility".  There is no "levelling up" or unlocking of bonuses in games like this - the only way to improve is for you to learn and get better!
Rouge System is a stunning one-man effort that even in early-access sits squarely at the pinnacle of its class, for space-flight simulations.

First of all - yeah, when I first started this game on my Win7 it had a twitchy picture and was virtually unplayable. My solution was to run it in windowed mode (via config file). Not a perfect way, but I've hardly seen any downsides.
Apart from that - don't get it wrong. It is a puzzle-puzzle game. It's short, it has next to nonexistent plot (which at the ending seems not only nearly nonexistent, but unnecessary as well). All in all - guys, it's not Myst, ok? It's a collection of assorted puzzles in a comfy environment. It will be a mistake to see it as anything but.
And so, the cornerstone of the game - puzzles. Puzzles are mostly really good. Some are quite inventive, some do a sort of unexpected play on widely known puzzle (like a famous pipeline puzzle with restricted movements, for instances) But, well, at the same time couple of puzzles are really dumb, while others just require decent amount of mix-and-match, which is not that fun. And of course, it can't be unmentioned - The confederate Cipher wheel WAS NOT used this way. It's a vanilla Caesar cipher in game! Come on, son! The whole point of cipher wheel is to scramble the letter statistics. Why can't you've used the proper codeword instead?! Oh, and a 6 moving pins puzzle is WAY too easy for it's own idea.
That said, other puzzles are fairly decent and inventive, though I've actually managed to solve 2 or 3 of them by semi-random clicking.
So there you have it, it's a compendium of puzzles set in a nicely drawn decor. Some are genuinely good, some are fairly stupid, some are unnecessary hard (that damn broken lock!). So pick it up on a sale cheap, go have your grey matter for a swing for an evening or two, but be cautious whether you'd manage to run it properly on a modern system.

Spoiler-free review, no worries.
Assuming it runs well on your machine, this game is actually quite fun. But before you get the game, a few things should be stated.
1. You do not roam freely around the house you have to explore. Instead, you click your way to waypoints, much like with Google Street View, and then have a 360° picture of your surroundings. Interactive objects, such as one of the many safes, can be simply clicked on.
2. The puzzles are hard, but (mostly) fair. I recommend having at least 3 sheets of paper and a pen beside you when playing. They will definitely come in handy. One thing to keep in mind is that you will not be told what is the expexted solution of the puzzles. Had to look up two of them because I simply didn't get what I was supposed to do.
3. A few of the puzzles are actually well-known. I immediately knew the answer to one of them simply because I've solved the exact same puzzle in another game and recognized the patterns of quite a few of them (
). Can be interpreted as positive or negative.
4. The story is, well, meh. I can see the devs really did put quite a bit of thought in how to fit the puzzles into the story, and did actually do a decent job at it, but the game is, in my opinion, mostly about the puzzles.
5. The ending leaves you slightly unsatisfied. No cut-scene or anything, just a text-based decision to make with a text-based outcome. Seems like the devs didn't want to put a lot more effort into creating an ending.
Nonetheless, it was a lot of fun while it lasted. The overall atmosphere is undisturbed and somehow inspirational, too. The music is sometimes a bit dark, but doesn't feel too displaced in any situation.
What I found strange was that the game wouldn't start if I switched the Steam language setting for this specific game to English. I had to play it in German - not much of a problem for me, but still kind of off-setting.
Oh, and one more thing ... if you're a diehard fan of smooth graphics with lots of effort in lighting and whatsoever, move on. This game clearly isn't for you.
In total, I'd give the game a solid 7/10. Worth buying if you like to spend a few relaxed hours with tackling some well designed puzzles, especially at this low price.

Deus Ex: Mankind Divided is a cyberpunk stealth action game set in the future version of Prague. Does it stealth its way to success or growls in frustration like its protagonist. Let's find out:
Deus Ex: Mankind Divided  puts you in the shoes of Adam Jensen, a gruff voiced protagonist who needs to solve a conspiracy which features the Illuminati. Deus Ex: Mankind Divided's story picks up right where the previous one ended with animosity growing between the augs and the humans. Let me get this out of the way first, I loved Human Revolution.
I felt that Human Revolution did the get the recognition when it was released due to much bigger releases in the year. Slowly, that game has garnered a strong following, so for Deus Ex: Mankind Divided to follow in the footsteps of such a game was a very difficult thing to do. But Mankind Divided pulls it off with flying colors. It is one of those games where you make your own path in each level.
The city of Prague in which the game is situated in is one of the best examples of quality over quantity. The city is so richly detailed and there are so many hidden routes throughout the city just waiting for you to explore them. Each path becomes clearer the more you look at them carefully. Mankind Divided is a game which rewards your curiosity.
The gameplay is where Mankind Divided truly shines. Each and every level is like a world of its own and that makes it infinitely replayable. In each playthrough there is some different way that misses your eye the first time around. Mankind Divided excells in its level designs. Add to that the huge amount of weapons and augs available to you and you can create a lot of stories on your own. Talking of the augs, they have received a upgrade too.
There are a lot more of these augmentations available this time around. They are fun and a blast to use. You can opt to use these and make your way stealthily or go all out Rambo on your enemies. Though by the time you unlock all of these augmentations you should be a walking Superman. That is where my biggest gripe with Mankind Divided  is. The game plays a  bit too easy in the later levels as the augmentations available to you make your enemies just fun distractions or more like targets on which you can practice your augmentations. The story is another place where Mankind Divided falters.
The story is short and comes to a very abrupt ending obviously making way for DLC or another sequel. The scope of the story is also very small unlike the game changing scenarios of the previous game. The gunplay is more solid than the previous game but still feels a bit loose. The characters themselves are fun and I really liked Adam Jensen and his allies. The city of Prague also tells a story of prejudice and discrimination with benches where it is clearly written that the augs are not allowed there. Though the story is short, there are a good amount of side quests available. All of these side quests are well done and feel connected to the main story and the struggle of the augs.
Mankind Divided  also features another mode called the Breach mode. This mode is like a Mankind Divided clone with bad SuperHot type graphics. It is an arcade type mode and features leaderboards to compete against your friends. All the microtransactions for the game are also attached mostly with this mode, so I did not have much trouble with them. Overall, Mankind Divided improves upon every bit of its marvelous predecessor even with its faltering story.
Graphically Mankind Divided is very good. The city of Prague looks absolutely phenomenal when you make your way through its streets. The character models are well done and there is a lot of variety in the environments. It absolutely nails the cyberpunk styled visuals it is going for. Especially on ultra settings, the sights are drop dead gorgeous and there are huge amounts of detail available in each frame.  There are a few lip syncing issues with characters and that sometimes takes you out of the immersion.
Deus Ex: Mankind Divided  features a superb sound design. With a really nice soundtrack which slowly builds up the atmosphere to the sudden change in mix because of your surroundings, everything is done very well. The voice acting is also one of the strong points of Mankind Divided. As I mentioned there are lip syncing issues but the voices are really good. Many people don't like the way Adam Jensen is voiced a.k.a. the christian bale's batman syndrome, but I really liked the way he talked. Overall, the sound of Mankind Divided  is a sweet package.
Deus Ex: Mankind Divided  is a game which improves upon every aspect of its predecessor except in the story division. It rewards your play style and has exceptional level designs. The city of Prague is gorgeous and densely packed. For those of you who are bored from the open world fatigue, Prague shows how much you can do in a little space. Deus Ex:Mankind Divided  is easily one of the best games this year and should not be overlooked.

Quick Summary: Torchlight 2 is a fun action RPG with gameplay very similar to Diablo 2 or the Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing. There is built in mod support for which you can download mods from the Steam workshop, and a ton of “end game” things like New Game + and Mapworks.
After the events of the first Torchlight game, the Alchemist (one of the heroes) has been corrupted by an artifact he took from the first game’s villain, and is planning to do all sorts of awful stuff. It’s up to 4 new heroes to follow and stop him before he unleashes a demonic invasion. It’s a pretty generic story (very similar to Diablo 2) with a few cartoony cutscenes. Most of the plot comes from conversations with quest giver NPCs, as you’d expect in an action RPG.
As mentioned earlier, the game is very similar in gameplay to Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing. You play in a third person isometric view and use your mouse buttons for attack/spell casting on hordes of monsters. Each class of character has 3 skill “tabs” but they aren’t conventional skill “trees” meaning none of the skills have prerequisites. You can also find scrolls that can be used to learn additional skills like healing or summoning spells. Interestingly, these scrolls can be used to teach skills to your “pet” (similar to like Katarina in the Van Helsing games). The pet can also be sent back to town to sell excess items, and provides a small presence in combat. Don’t count on the pet to do any real killing or tanking though (unlike Katarina).
Anyone familiar with ARPG games will know how the randomly generated loot and levels work, and just like the first Torchlight game, there is a lot of socketable “ember” to be found. Ember is like the gems in Diablo 2, and can be added to equipment with sockets to provide bonuses like + damage or +% resistance (depending on if it goes into a weapon or an armor). There are a number of “unique” or “set” loot items as well as “legendaries” which are uber rare and can take a hundred hours of grinding to find. Your inventory stash is rather limited, but you do have the option to share items between characters.
Pros:
+Multiplayer co-op for the campaign, and the loot is individualized so don’t worry about someone stealing your item drops.
+The game is pretty long (about 16 hours) and there is a lot to do, even after you beat the story. You can play the New Game + (start the game over with all your items and skills) or you can play the Mapworks, which randomly generates levels. You can only find the legendary items in New Game +.
+For a game with so much content, the download size is remarkably small. It’s also not very hardware intensive, but the graphics are still pretty good.  You can also download player made mods from the steam workshop to mix things up even more.
Cons:
-The game can get very grindy, especially if you’re going for some of the Steam achievements.  Some of them (like selling 50k items to merchants) will likely take hundreds of hours playing.
-The respec system is very limited. You can only reset the last 3 skill points you put in, so if you want to try different builds, you need to start a new character. You can use console commands to fully respec, but that marks your character as a cheater in online play.
Overall the game is very good but by the time you finish the first playthrough you probably will want to take a break. I played the rather overpowered spell caster character and my fingers hurt by the end of the game. I didn’t really feel like going into New Game +. I can only imagine what it would be like playing through with a melee fighter that has to sit there swinging at each enemy. In comparison, I played through the Incredible Adventures of Van Helsing back to back with all 3 character classes (though that game was significantly shorter).
Do you like Diablo? Do you like dungeon crawlers? Do you like good things? Then Torchlight II is for you! The learning curve is very short for average gamers. You can't go wrong.

Whew, boy. Brawlhalla.
Where to begin with this game.
Next month, I'll have been playing this game for a full year. I've decided to wait this long to post this review solely because I want it to be based on actual experience with the game, and not "i played for a few hours, here's what i didn't like, here's what i do like."
While at first glance, Brawlhalla may appear to be a Smash Bros clone for PC, but i assure you, it's far from it. In fact, the only similar mechanic is racking up damage to knock the enemy off screen.
From simple Speed Dodging to Gravity Cancelling, Brawlhalla can be played by anyone as long as they are willing to learn!
The game features a wide and unique variety of weapons and characters to choose from, and there are tons of ways to play with said weapons and characters.
The combat is fluid, hitboxes are (for the most part) within a reasonable size, and best of all it's FREE.
No, none of that "it's free but spend money to actually be good" nonsense. 100% FREE.
However, the game does have an in-game store called Mallhalla (HA) where you can trade real money for in-game currency called "Mammoth Coins." Mammoth Coins are one of the 3 currencies in Brawlhalla, among Gold, Mammoth Coins, and Glory. Gold is awarded by simply playing the game, completing daily missions, and logging in consecutively. Mammoth Coins can ONLY be aquired by buying them, and Glory is awarded to players at the end of a ranked season based on their performance in both Ranked 1v1 and Ranked 2v2 over the season.
Mammoth Coins can buy you characters, but why do that when you can buy characters with Gold? or just simply buy the All Characters Pack for $20 on Steam?
Mammoth Coins serve one sole purpose: Purchasing Cosmetics. No pay to win items, nothing changes how you play the game, it changes how you LOOK. Taunts, Character Skins, Weapons Skins, KO Effects, Sidekicks and Avatars are what you'll be spending your Mammoth Coins on. Unfortunately, this game does run solely on profit from the optional currency, so the cosmetics are a BIT overpriced. But there are new items on sale every week, so you can save a bit of MC.
Now off of the store, we move onto the game's issues. Nothing is without it's flaws, and believe me, Brawlhalla certainly has it's fair share.
Most of the earlier legends are a bit broken, and were sadly never fixed. taking Cassidy's Down Signature, Roland as a whole, and Hattori's sword as examples, there are more than a few things that are easy to get hit by.
The game's netcode is great, unless your internet runs into a bump. You can be comboing the enemy into oblivion, feeling great, only to see the next second you're at the bottom of the screen, no chance of recovering, and your opponent pulls off a taunt to spite you. These are called rollbacks, and they are insanely ridiculous. Hell, they're the reason i got so mad my PC's screen broke.
Combo Weapons such as Sword, Katars and Gauntlets have far more strengths than weaknesses. I've heard multiple complaints, and experienced it myself, enough times to hear "Nerf Sword/Katars/Gauntlets" on almost a daily basis.
And finally, it is INFURIATING. Getting on a loss streak is very upsetting in this game because of someone not dying, using moves over and over, or simply losing because of uncontrollable circumstances.
Brawlhalla is a GREAT fighting game, a great way to satisfy your hunger for a great competitive title, and an AWESOME time killer for casuals who just want to punch their friends in the face.
I definitely recommend it.

The three heroes slowly discover the path out of this mysterious place while someone is observing their progress through a magic mirror...
There is also a DLC called "The Goblin Menace". If you are unsure if you want to buy this game, I can totally recommend it! This game is a bit hard to determine... I have to say it most definantly has it's pros and cons to it.  Now I can't say first off that I'd always recommend it, although I have in the past and with the right person might in the future.  But there are some things that have disappointed me before and I do say Turbine is one of the greedier of the mmorpg companies I've seen.
For one, you have to pay in this game or you hit a serious level wall.  Yes, there are ways to level up and never pay a dime, but it takes some serious work and hard to even get past level 40 that way. (I've tried, trust me)  In the begining of the game, you start out with some decent but lore breaking.  Of course, not everyone is as into lore as me so if you don't care too much about Tolkien's lore or don't know much about that, then you don't have to worry.  But if you're like me and you do, it might make you cringe a bit.  However, that isn't enough to completely down this game.
Once you get out of the introduction, you enter the game either in Archet, the Shire, or Ered Luin depending on race.  Then you start the very long, very boring quests in this game.  The main questline, although once again can break lore from time to time, is not too bad and can even be very fun at times.  However, almost all of the side quests are very similar and somewhat boring.  Although I have found they do differ from location to location on what you do.  I personally go with Ered Luin intro quests no matter what race I choose just because it is the most enjoyable scenery in my opinion.  Once you complete your starting zones, you move to Bree (which is my least favorite place to quest) and the Barrow Downs.  Afterwards you move on into the Lone Lands which is considerably enjoyable region in itself to quest until you do it 5/6/20 times.  This is where you hit the level wall.  After Lonelands, you cannot do any quests save for the main storyline without buying expansion packs to the next region.  However, questing isn't the only way to level.
Of course in LOTRO you have crafting.  You can only choose three crafting sections such as tailoring, woodworking, forestry, prospecting, farming, cooking, metalworking, and scholar (feel like I'm forgetting someone).  You gain xp everytime you craft and you increase your craft level just lik almost any mmorpg.  That's pretty generic.
My favorite part of this game is instances and skirmishes that you can either solo or do in a fellowship (party).  This game is quite fun with their BD (Barrow-Downs) instance line as well as their skirms such as Trouble in Tuckborough and Seige of Gondamon.  Later on in the game they began adding in epic battles which you had to pay for, however these epic battles were very much worth it with a very unique fighting style that does please the lore side of me.
So without paying, I've found it's hard to go past lvl 40, but it is worth paying for the epic battles and such in my opinion.   That is, if you can find the right kinship (guild).
Now lets move away from the game as a game.  So if you're not an rper, the rest of this review does not relate to you.
Lord of the Rings Online has a enormous lore base. If you want to rp, you must read the Lord of the Rings trilogy and the Hobbit at the least for the game theoretically follows those storylines and the rp is set in that time period.  But you must also know that the game use to have the strongest rules for lore, especially the Elvish rp community.  Magic is not a common norm for most rps, at least on the Laurelin RP server. (which I recommend if you choose to rp on this game).  There are large scale rp kinships and a very active hub at the Prancing Pony that almost always has at least 1 rper.  One characteristic that makes the rp on this game specifically nice is that you can turn on rp tag, which turns your name white so that any other rper can identify you as a rper ready for random rp at any time.  This game also has long costume emotes with /e and many other emotes to go along with it. (More can be bought on the Turbine store)
Now I've played on this game for almost four years now, and have to admit at the moment I'm disappointed in the rp communities direction.  However, this game tends to swing around again and go from bad to good back to bad back to good.  So it's never a game I'd completely give up, but at times I may not recommend it to another rper while other times I may.  I do love this game's website for rpers,
.  If you ever rp on this game, you have to go there to find the right kinship, rp storylines, friends, and so on with.

This game is amazingly tactile for the lack of 'game content' that it has right now. Even though there's only a single ship to use at the time of this review, it's an amazing challenge in itself. This is one of those games like the ones of old where you're begging for a manual because jesus christ that was a 30-step-plus checklist and I need to be able to write it down.
The idea that everything you're running is backed up by a simulation engine - not scripting workarounds - is an incredible difference in behavior of everything you do. It's very subtle but noticeable when you play this game and realize that yes, everything in the checklist is important and you really need to pay attention in the tutorial.
What makes this game super exciting for me is the idea that multi-crewed ships are currently on the wishlist - I've played lots of multi-crewed games and due to their simplistic nature you can always manage to find a way to make the game dull and monotonous with a competent-enough crew. The way this game is being built the excitement will truly be a thing of beauty because you will actually have to guess how best to fix a problem - if/when the manual fails you - by using your knowledge of the systems that are on your ship and you can and most likely will be wrong the first time. You'll end up in situations that you're going to end up having to do complex, multiple subsystem troubleshooting while in the process of trying to avoid dying painfully in the void of space.
If this game takes off I think it could definitely change the way that space combat sims that have an eye towards more of the sim part will fundamentally approach their solutions.
On an interesting note, currently this game is less than a gig upon install. That's an interesting thing to me in itself. Kudos to the developer!

This is a game that brings back a lot of memories.
A quick note for those curious about this game. If you're expecting a tie-in with Tron Legacy, brace for disappointment on that front as this game long predates that movie. HOWEVER, don't overlook this game because of it. It's a great spin-off of the original Tron movie and definately worth the playthrough.
The game puts you in control of Jet Bradley, the adult son of Alan and Laura Bradley from the original movie, although Laura has since passed away. Jet gets digitized into the computer by Ma3a, Alan's AI assistant, when a powerful computer virus gets into the ENCOM network and Alan disappears. However, as expected, there's a lot more than a mere virus at work.
The game itself is an FPS, giving you control of a disc from the original Tron movie along with other weapons. In total, there are 12 different weapons, four of which you can have equipped at all times once acquired although the disc will be your go-to in most cases. The game's equipment and leveling mechanics are unique too. You can insert different utility, weapon, and armor devices into a sort of loadout ring at any time but each item takes up a certain number of slots. Luckily items can be upgraded to provide more power and take up less space. Each item can be upgraded twice, starting at Alpha, upgrading to Beta, and finally to Gold. You can also find beta and gold level items in the wild too so choose which abilities to upgrade wisely.
The leveling mechanic is interesting as well, as you must find build points scattered around each level. A counter on your HUD tells you how many points are on each level and how many you've found. Every ten points you earn is considered a level up and  allows you to go in and upgrade your stats.
Oh, and did I mention the Light Cycles? A good portion of the game features light cycle matches, using both the original light cycles from Tron and the new Super Light Cycle in 3D rendered light cycle arenas. There are even a few Light Cycle arenas you can play outside of the main story.
A word to the wise, the quicksave button is your friend. There are no checkpoints to speak of so save early, and save often, because dying can cause you to lose some valuable progress and might even force you to start a level from the beginning.
So if you're interested in a non-canon spinoff to the original Tron movie as well as a great FPS, this is a game for you.

This game is just full of nostalgia, being wonderfully referencial to both its source material and 90's/00's 'hacker' fiction in general. The combat is the main gameplay, this being an FPS and all. This means you can find a lot of interesting stuff you don't make any sense off in the start but will make sense when you have to go there for the main quest or a sidequest. This really helpes making the World feel free for the taking and immersive.
There are also a lot of added improvements on previous Deus Ex titles when it comes to exploring, you no longer need to remember or write down codes you find. If you find a code for a locker, that code will show when you try to open it. Even if the mail where you found the code didn't tell you exactly which locker the code is for or where it is the system wil automatically tell you the code if you have it. This is a great improvement because writting down codes or "trying" codes on different places to see which code opens which door are naught but time sinks, boring and detracts from he fun of the exploring.
The game will also tell you anytime you enter an area where enemies will attack you on sight, this makes the game much more fun to play and explore because you no longer have to worry about getting shot in the back when you are exploring unless you are exploring an area that is actually dangerous. Less of the "breaking in-getting shot by guy you didn't see/didn't know was agro-load the game and repeat". The game warns you if you need to keep out of sight and it gives room for less frustration, less time sinks and more fun time.
I've talked at length about the strength of the game, however it has many glaring weaknesses that makes it so I cannot recommend it. In my view it has mainly two huge ones.
- The game is extremely easy, even on the hardest difficulty you can have (without having cleared the game) the game is a cake walk. I played it on hardest and followed a couple of tips I read online(kotaku) on what you should know Before starting to play the game. I played without every buyingt the invisibility augment, without getting the social augment(which shows the correct answers when discussing) and without using any omnitool(automatically hack stuff). All this to make the game harder than it was to give me a slight challenge and yeah it was a slight one indeed. The game is a stealth game that gives you A LOT of ways to bypass enemies, invis your way by enemies(if you get the aug) or simply kill your enemies. Whichever way you choose to go its easy. I will say the maps are very well designed but your character is way too OP or the enemies are way too UP or both.
- A Deus Ex game to me is about choice, its as much about the gameplay as it is about the story and the choices you can make and to be frank the ropeplaying "decisions" you can make in this game are very very weak. The main plot is also weak in itself and this really puts a dent in what I think of this game.
I will say the now in my closing that the sidequests are really awesome and give meaningful and interesting choice and they are fun. Sadly I can't say the same thing of the main game, I liked the game because I got stuck in the exploring and the sidequests and I loved that part of the game but if you either want a challenge gameplay wise or great/interesting story with roleplay elements maybe you should reconsider buying this game.

Oh, man.  Human Revolution is just about my favourite game ever, I've played through it several times, but I've got to tell you, having just 'finished' this, I'm feeling a bit let down.  I'm still marking this review in blue because it IS really good, what's here, but I have to agree with other reviewers that say this really is only the beginning of the plot.  Even the trailers for this game that I've been hanging on the edge of every second of since it was announced suggested that you were going to be able to do a lot more, that much of the banter that gets tossed around throughout the dialog of this game was actually going to become material to the plot.  Credits rolled right after I'd defeated who I thought was just the first main boss of a long, deeply considered game like HR. I was shocked.
That more of this is coming in a DLC context? Okay.  I played HR after story DLC was already released for it, all as one, but I definitely would have preferred to know that this was going to be 'episodic' in nature.  I would have still signed on gladly, and probably been pleased to know that there was going to be more to look forward to in the future, but feeling a little mislead by the marketing of the game has left a little bit of a bad taste in my mouth that is definitely going to carry over into caveats when I talk about the game to others.
I did like the setup of new skills and options, and also that the system wasn't completely different from Human Revolution. I could go through playing more or less the way I'm used to, what I got good at especially during the first couple of play-throughs of the first game (hide in vent, shoot people in the knees, profit; I'm not a big FPS person and I'm not terribly good at them as a rule).  It's also going to make this shorter-than-I-wanted game more fun to go back and replay, choosing different options and trying to make other things work.  I also appreciated the instances in the game where I had to make an irrevocalble choice one way or another.  In some, you're warned, taking one quest over another and knowing that you can't go back and pick up the other pieces you let fall.  Others just happened.  Both of these dynamics will make going back to explore different areas of the story a lot more satisfying, so from that point of view, they did a great job.
As a writer, I'm shaking my head; I strenuously dislike, in any media, the feeling that something only got made to set up a sequel.  There's worse examples of this out there in the world, but it's a big let down following how richly developed the plot of Human Revolution was.

Let me start by saying that I'm a huge fan of Human Revolution, finished it at least 3 times and would probably play again. I was looking forward to Mankind Divided for months, after the initial reviews I'd waited for a sale and got it for half price. Even considering that...I'm still disappointed.
It feels like a slightly visually-improved HR, with half the plot and a serious lack of polishing.
(I feel like I should also say that I've just recently finishied my 200-hour-long gameplay of Witcher 3, and the fact that Mankind Divided is selling for €50 - the same price as The Witcher 3 with all of it's DLCs - is just plain mindboggling.)
Things that bothered me, in no particular order:
- the metro - why WHY? there are only four places to go, why not make it a one open area? and don't even get me started on the loading times. I would click travel and then browse the internet on my phone in the meantime. at least give us something to read while we wait, like most of the games do.
- lazy area design. I've seen some praises for the level design and while I'd agree when it comes to Golem City or Palisade Bank, but Prague itself? almost every apartment, basement, bathroom and shop looks basically the same! considering the scale of the city, which is not so big, there could be a little more variation - make the exploration more rewarding, instead of turning it into loot-seeking. I had to consult the map until the end of the game because everything looked so similar...
- the phone app breaks immersion. while I don't mind the phone app itself, or the content behind the triangles, it was not appropriate for the first playthrough of the game. why not add it just to the game+ ? I played though HR Director's Cut with devs commentary on my 3rd playthrough and enjoyed the behind-the-scenes perspective while exploring thing I'd already seen before. no one want to stop and listen to developers talking, while they're experiencing the plot for the first time.
- you can't jump in moving elevators, what's up with that?
- you can't combine two groups of the same thing in the inventory (even when it amounts to less than 25).
- jumping over sth from behind a cover is the stupidest thing ever. if there's nothing to hide behind, Jensen just barrels forward a few steps and straight into the fire. good times.
- NPCs. there are not enough interactions with secondary characters to make me care about any of them. I cared more about the cat-lady's plot than about McReady, for example. all in all, the side missions had more meaningfull emotional impact than the main plot. not a good sign.
- new augs. Jensen continues to be pumped full of experimental tech and everything works out just fine because he's a special snowflake. but where did they come from? we just don't know. they are just there and they're pretty much useless if you're doing a stealth playthrough. the only one I'd been using is the remote hacking (it's awesome), and TESLA I used maybe twice.
- the language. I happen to be Polish, and Polish language is largely similar to Czech. while in general, I feel they did a good job of making in-game Czech believable, it annoyed me when obviously Czech characters pronounced Czech names with English accents.
- performance. I started playing only after the first patches, but still, the frame-drops persist and cause much frustration.
- I miss the orange.
- what's up with Eliza Cassan? I feel like that side mission should have more of an impact. thanks for ruining my stealth approach btw.
- the ending is a joke.
- forcing a player to sit through the credits is a double joke.
There are some things that I liked though:
- the side missions
- that one chubby "lady of the night"
- reasonable female clothes
- the score
- voice acting
- Jensen walking around shirtless
- the entire Golem City part
- ???
All in all, I'm just sad. I love the universe, I love the Montreal crew and I'm sure they put a lot of work into this. I really wanted to love this game. While I don't hate it either, I wouldn't recommend it for the full price.
I will be giving this game another chance, maybe when I'm not so bitter, and will come back to this review later.

The good:
- More and interesting augs
- The back story and the universe
- Good sidemissions. Even when I give them critic that they are long, they are good.
- Good amount of weapons
- Good amount of variety to complete the mission
- This is definitely a Deus Ex game
- Graphics, aesthetics and feel. The world feels like it happened after the previous Deus Ex
- If you go crazy the game resets after a situation change.
Arguable (depends on your view):
- I miss the clear bad guy lv. + boss fights. What I mean with this, is that in the previous one, the cities where narrative build that usually followed a "boss base + boss fight". It is arguable is there more than one boss fight.
- Consequences didn't have a clear effect in my opinion. It didn't come up much even when I knocked out all the police in the streets. This however is arguable because then again it can be seen as protecting the player from f:ing up the game.
The "bad":
- There isn't as much variety to the environments compared to before but you mainly stay in Prag.
- The side missions can be long and with it, they can take too much focus from the main storyline making you feel like: Ok, side mission done, where was I in the main story??
- The killing vs. not killing affects the story rather superficially
- Micropayments, not because they are mandatory, they are not, but because they bring one-time usable items in a single-player game. I personally feel that single-player games should not have use once items. They can have micro-DLC's like skins etc. but you should have access to them.
- The "kill them all" option is much much easier than the silent option. I haven't tried this on the hardest level, but I played the game on: Give me Deus Ex and in this level, taking out enemies with additional mech armored troops and drones was relatively easy.
- If you knocked out everyone in a district there is no consequence that would make your life hard. Example: you would be a wanted man forcing you to avoid cops.
Common critic:
Bugs
I have had the game crash a few times and sometimes loading a game takes loooong (like 5 - 10min). Also, likely due to the Dx12 setting, sometimes if you try to return to Windows the game won't let go of the 3D card and simply make the display go black or not even leave (sometimes its black but the sounds like the UX effects can be heard).
All that said, non of these bugs really made the game any less good. Just sometimes (above was rare) made me wait. That said, people have experienced some wild bugs.
Micropayments
The micropayments don't come in your way and are not at all forced. The annoying thing about them is that some of the special edition stuff is usable only once. This sucks because I explicitly buy single-player games so that I can replay them with different combinations. Example: MassEffect has micro DLC's (skins etc). But what makes the more of micro DLS instead of micropayments is that you can use them as many times as you want. Example: The elite version of the Rifle can be picked from your storage only once, after that it is associated to that save game only. Bye bye replay with that rifle.

If anyone ever asked me – "There's so many Hack&Slash ARPGs on the market now, what's special about this one?" - then I would had answered without a blink – "It's mods". Torchlight 2 was the first of it's genre to get a steam workshop support, which is, coupled with how incredibly easy making simple mods in TL2 is, attracted a lot of modder wannabes, so we now have steam workshop overflowing with all kinds of mods. Probably the most common is class mods – I think I'd stopped counting at 30 differently named classes, some standalone, some were part of mod packs. There are also plenty of other mods – UI/HUD mods, pet mods, fishing mods, mods that increase exp or gold gain, mods that increase drops, mods that increase drop quality, and even a few overhauls and new location mods.
Don't get me wrong – I'm not really a mod enthusiast. It's just vanilla game is average at best. One of the key features of Torchlight series is it's difficulty settings. Torchight 2 has four – casual, normal, veteran and elite. While in pretty much every other hack&slash game a player progresses through difficulties, this one utilizes a classical approach - you pick the difficulty at start and stick with it. What's known as difficulty in other games is just New Game+, New Game++, and New Game+++ here. The difference between, say, casual and elite is that at latter monsters do 4 times more damage than the former. And this completely breaks half of game mechanics. It leads to player receiving way too much damage, with "one-shots" as an extreme (almost guaranteed in TL2 on elite).
The way to minimize oneshots is gearing for survivability. And this is one of the TL2's major shortcomings – no matter what build you play you pretty much always gear for survivability. Variability? Nope! Because of that loot is broken – majority of unique items does not provide you with it, so one would prefer a randomly generated item with +health instead. And, as this isn't bad enough, loot in TL2 is scarce. So scarce that visiting a shop will easily replace clearing two or three dungeons. Pretty sure at least 90% of my gear came from shop while I was playing on elite difficulty. Quite often I just used a certain technique to reroll a shop ("shopfarming") simply because a) it's much faster and yields more stable results than farming monsters, and b) you need this gear to progress through the game. If this is not a faulty design then what is?!
There's plenty of mythos about this game circulating on forums and cultivated by the community. One of them is that TL2 is rich on character builds. Let's not count casual/normal, because pretty much everything works there. I would be challenged to name more than 3 good builds for each class for beginners wishing to play on elite. The cause of that is classes being full of "utility" skills that suit any build, as well as some underwhelming skills that are just never taken, so if you try to play optimally your builds will end up being very similar, in some cases the difference is just the skill you spam to do damage. E.g., the difference between engineer using a cannon and engineer using a 2handed melee weapon is exactly this.
This is pretty much why plenty of people on forum will tell you to just install some mods. Ironic, but most mods just attempt to throw in more low quality content or bandaid-fix existing problem, so the issues above persist even in modded game.
Among the things I really want to praise in TL2 is dynamic, fast paced combat that'll punish you if you're not paying enough attention. I consider TL2 to be the most action-oriented game of the genre. It's also pretty cool that in TL2 trash monsters matter – some of them are very capable to be the case of your character's demise.
Overall, I think Torchlight 2 doesn't deserve it's Overwhelmingly Positive rating in steam. TL2, being released early autumn 2012, certainly owes a lot of it's popularity to initial failure of Diablo 3 and being the only fresh enough alternative. But, the year is 2016 now, TL2's prime is long over, and  it is just a somewhat decent ARPG, forsaken by developers, but still floating because of mods, low price tag and being not online-only.
Do I recommend this game? Hard to say. But I certainly can't downvote it, having played it so much.

is a clicker/idle game with a cute anime aesthetic. If you enjoy courting beautiful women then this game is probably right up your alley. Despite using a generic clicker game model, there is also a bit of dating sim action as you have to raise your stats, work jobs and go on dates with your ladies as well give them gifts. The game offers a wide variety of waifus and more to come.
In this game you play a nameless generic character, each route gives you some backstory on how you met the girls. Usually you end up crashing into them or making them upset in some way and you then have to atone for your actions. The girls all have different personalities and you can talk to them or click on them to get more dialogue. The story is very simple, though it does offer a good bit of comedy and even some meme humor.
The game is mostly an idler, your main objective is to raise a girl’s affection level and progress in your relationship with her. You can also click on the girls to raise her affection levels or chat with her. The dating simulation aspect comes from raising your stats which are then used to get jobs to earn money. Your stats also matter when it comes to the girls as her affection level won’t raise via idling unless you have a certain stat, a good example is Quill. You unlock her early on but cannot raise her affection via idling unless you have the Luck stat which you don’t unlock until later. Money comes into play in letting you buy your lady friend gifts or take her out on dates. To get to the next relationship level with a girl you’re often required to meet a few different criteria, like giving her certain gifts or taking her on certain dates or even have a a stat raised to an expressed level.
Raising the girls’ relationship levels offers new artwork of the girls-to-be scene and all the artwork is easy on the eyes. Many of the girls are very busty and a lot of the artwork depicts them in a sexy way. If you enjoy anime then the artstyle will work for you. All of the user interfaces in the game are bright and colorful, and everything is easy to read.  There is no voice acting in the game and the background music in the game is all the same. There are some sound effects in the game but nothing extraordinary.
+ Very addictive and fun.
+ Good graphics and audio.
+ Beautiful women to court with great anime aesthetics and fulfilling to your waifu needs.
+ Steam achievements and trading cards.
+ It’s free to play.
- Can take quite a bit of time to progress with a lady.
- Some requirements to woo a lady are very over the top.
- Microtransactions.
As an anime fan and a lover of beautiful ladies I really enjoyed this game. It’s a fun time waster and can be left idling for quite a while. I imagine this game is geared more towards male gamers due to the sexy nature of the women but I didn’t mind at all. The game developers are actively listening to the community and improving things in the game which shows promise for when the game leaves the Early Access stage.

This is not a game for everybody, but I LOVED it. As other reviewers are saying, it won't hold your hand--the puzzles are pretty darn difficult and usually don't explain themselves. But that's the appeal for me. It's like I really get to be a detective in some movie or something, and I have nothing but my wits to go on. The downside to the difficulty is, of course, you WILL get frustrated from time to time--pretty often, in fact, so if you don't like scratching your head too much, this isn't your game. But the difficulty of the puzzles and having to figure out even what you have to do to figure them out means that you get a huge rush from solving them. Not joking, the satisfaction of solving these things is great, makes ya feel like an extra-special clever lil cupcake. Beating the game made me feel like a genius.
I do want to point out, someof the puzzles require you to give up on the room you're working through, try another route, then come back when you've gained a clue or insight from somewhere later in the game. If you have to come back to a puzzle, it doesn't mean you've failed, and you're probably doing what you're actually supposed to by saving it for later.
The problems I did have were mostly interface ones: when you do get a verbal clue from your character, it is only ever said once, and there's no way of it being logged in a Notes menu or anything, so if you go AFK for a minute at the wrong time or don't have your sound turned on, you can miss the hint completely. The hints usually aren't going to be crucial to solving a given puzzle, though. Also, I wished it was easier to move around the house; because the game is a point-and-click, you walk down hallways by clicking your mouse in the direction you want to go, and the screen changes to the part of the room you're in as you move. There is a map in your menu that gets marked off when you solve the puzzle in that room, and I wanted to be able to "fast-travel" or something similar by clicking on the room I wanted to go to, instead of having to go through the whole house one scene-frame at a time. It IS a point-and-click from the early-2000s, though, so not a lot to be expected there.
Overall, I loved the game, and when I was done, I went and bought another whole package of point-and-click puzzlers from the same company, I liked it so much!

Every time there's a new Mortal Kombat, you're probably going to hate it for a while. The mechanics are never copy/pasted over and you have to essentially learn a new game. So after I forced myself to get humiliated and destroyed for two weeks I finally have the hang of it and love it. If you liked every other MK, particularly 9, this will grow on you eventually. Everythings improved.

MKX(L) is an insanely-fun fighting game until you face Liu Kang and his stupid windmill punches.
I've never been a big fan of the Mortal Kombat series since its inception in 1992 (oh was the fever for it HUGE), but I've never truly disliked it, either.  I have always been drawn to its over-the-top lunacy and its marriage of kung fu fantasy and comic book storylines.  The fact that it has survived the fall of Midway and ended up being quite stronger than it has ever been is testament to the franchise and Ed Boon's insane loyalty to it (25 years and counting).  Having grown up a Street Fighter and KoF fan, MK's button layout and combo-centric gameplay coupled with its weird digitized people thing always kept me at arm's reach.  Still, any time a new title would come out, at least up until Trilogy, I would dump some quarters in and give it a go.  Once the franchise left the arcades and went into the home, I was pretty much done with it except perhaps to read up on some of that fun, convoluted lore.  There was always some interest, but man, those 3D fighters did not look like fun.  It wasn't until MK9 when I was called back to it because, quite simply, EVERYONE was talking about it.  And it was good!  It was still combo-centric and it still had a kind of weird button layout, but there was significantly less cheese (except in the case of Liu Kang... man, ♥♥♥♥ that guy) and it was thoroughly fun and engaging.  It was also a reboot, so I didn't really need to know why so-and-so was dead and so-and-so was no longer eating meat.
Which brings us to MKX(L).  As a relative MK noob, I stay clear from online play because getting your♥♥♥♥♥kicked 100% of the time isn't a fun, so I play mostly single player as a filthy casual.  Aside from the ridculous "epic" that is the story mode (basically a really long goofy movie peppered with some fights for you to play out), MKX(L) offers a tremendous amount of content for the non-competitive cazz, such as myself.  Classic ladder modes like the Towers are present, so if you've played any of the original 3, you know exactly what you're getting into (as a bonus, characters still get endings even though the story focus is the story mode), plenty of challenges, and even a fun on-going faction war where you play vs. the AI, but contribute to an overall pool of points among five factions made up of every player.  Choosing a faction allows you to gain some bonuses and unlock some fatalities called faction kills and simply playing against the AI will earn you points to level up.  Despite the tremendous amount of DLC content, there's still a lot of stuff to discover and unlock such as costumes and finishing moves as you fiddle with each character.  People can downvote the DLC bomb all they want, but it's precisely why I don't buy games like this on release.
At any rate, the game looks and plays great and most of the move sets are quite similar to each other, so it's not like you need to get a degree in each character in order to play well.  I play with a stick, but if you've got a good d-pad (read: not the 360 controller), then this plays just fine with a controller.  Playing through story mode will get your feet wet with pretty much every character available in the base game and though it's a long journey, once you're done you will probably have a good idea of which characters you like best.  From there, head on into training mode and get comfortable with combo play because that's the name of the game.  Where I consider Street Fighter to be a tactical-response kind of brawler with a lot of back and forth, I would categorize MK as a jousting style kind of game where you clash a lot, but once someone falls off the horse, it's pretty much over.  Still, landing a tremendous unblockable combo string is immensely satisfying and despite dropping 11 hits in one go, it's not all that devastating to be on the receiving end (unless it's Liu Kang's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ windmill punches).  The AI is quite forgiving until you bump it up.  Try the hardest level or fighting a faction boss in the "war" mode and you'll find MK2-levels of ultimate cheese (for those who don't know - MK2 was notorious for being cheap).  In-line with this jousting concept, you should be aware that your inputs can often feel sluggish, but not because they actually are, but more because the nature of the combo gameplay means that whiffing hard means you're not going to recover like you would in other fighters.  You'll have to reprogram yourself if you're like me, simply to get used to that recovery time before trying anything again.  Once you get used to it, the game is lightning fast, but knowing the combos is going to make your life much easier - some characters are not so noob-friendly and you'll find it hard to string along hits if you don't already know the sequence.
What I really enjoy about this game, above its fantastic graphics, characters, and over-the-top gore.... is its sound design.  If you have the opportunity to pump this game through a sound system with a hefty subwoofer, you will find that MKXL -sounds- fun.  Anyone who hears you (if anyone is around to hear, of course) will instantly wonder wtf is going on and come see.  The hits all have that Hollywood-style thump'n'crack and the game is so good at audibly providing information like just how hard a punch or kick lands.  It is a joy to listen to and adds so much to the game.  The sound here, at least to me, really feels like what Dead Space did for shooters, MKXL does for fighters.  Go look up a video if you need to, but trust me that this game sounds awesome and in a series where characters don't typically call out their moves, there's enough ear candy here to get your blood pumping.
As for technical stuff, I have not encountered a single bug or crash, but granted, NRS and the WB had plenty of time to iron those things out before I got to it.  Game runs smoothly and just fine.  Initially I perceived a lot of input lag, but I don't really feel that's the case anymore.  My only true recommendation is to find an alternative to the 360 controller if that's all you have - the stick is too weird to play with and the d-pad has always, always sucked a big sweaty fat one.
